item.title: As Giants pursue Jonathan Taylor, could they pivot to Derrick Henry?
item.description: Quarterback injuries could prompt Baltimore to listen to offers for Henry.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants (and other teams) hope to land Colts running back Jonathan Taylor via trade. With Baltimore's season potentially falling apart following Sunday injuries to starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) and his backup Tyler Huntley (toe), there could be another running back to potentially be pursued at or before the November 10 deadline, by the Giants or other teams.

Derrick Henry, now 32, is far closer to the end of his career than the beginning. His contract pays out $12 million in 2027, with none of it guaranteed.

Now could be the time for the Ravens to turn the remainder of his contract into a draft pick or two.

And the Giants would make plenty of sense. Beyond the fact that the Giants view Taylor as on the second tier of current NFL tailbacks with Henry, Giants coach John Harbaugh has experience with Henry.

After a Week 5 loss to the Saints, Harbaugh explained the distribution of carries to a wide swath of tailbacks by pointing out that they don't have a clear-cut workhorse.

“I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance,” Harbaugh said at the time. “A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be."

The best way to be in a "Derrick Henry circumstance" would be to, you know, get Derrick Henry.

Whether the Ravens would trade Henry depends on whether they plan to keep him beyond this season. If they'd cut him before a $1 million roster bonus comes due in March, they wouldn't get a compensatory draft pick. The only way to get value for his contract would be to trade it.

Through eight games, Henry leads the league with 158 carries. He has 632 yards (4.0 per carry) and eight touchdowns.

Given the quarterback injuries in Baltimore, the Ravens surely will get a call or two about Henry. The Giants, given their interest in Taylor, could be one of them.

item.title: Bears at Seahawks: 3 Props to Play
item.description: The Chicago Bears face the Seattle Seahawks on MNF. Here are props to play featuring JSN, Luther Burden, Kalif Raymond, and Jeffery Simmons.
item.content:encoded:
I feel like it’s been a long time since I’ve written up a props article. Probably because it’s been a week and a half since the Bears faced the Patriots. We had a good week last week; 2 out of 3 ain’t bad, and that raised our season record to 10-11.

This week, the Bears have a massive game against the Seattle Seahawks. Both teams are looking to show they are one of the elite teams in the NFC and ready to push for the Super Bowl. The Bears made a huge impact move by trading for Jeffery Simmons this past week, and he is expected to play. Let’s look at the prop plays for this week. As always, odds courtesy of FanDuel.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba OVER 99.5 Receiving Yards -113

You hate to lead off the prop plays with a Seattle over, but how do you not expect JSN to gain significant yardage? He’s gained over 100 yards in every game but one this year, and you can’t look at the Bears’ current crop of cornerbacks and think it’s a good matchup for Chicago. The only hope is that with Simmons in the mix, Dennis Allen blitzes less and Kyler Gordon has some success against him. Other than that, you have to expect at least 2 or 3 pretty sizable gains from JSN and another day over 100 yards receiving.

Luther Burden OVER 52.5 Receiving Yards -113

In the two games since Caleb Williams’ return, Burden has caught all 12 targets he’s gotten from Caleb for a total of 225 yards and a touchdown. Burden has easily taken over WR1 status in Chicago with Caleb back in the fold, and he should see some shallow crossers tonight with an opportunity to gain some yards after the catch similarly to what happened against New England.

Kalif Raymond OVER 16.5 Receiving Yards -113

This last one was between Raymond and Sam Roush. With Cole Kmet out for the year, there’s a hole, albeit a small one, in the Bears offense, and you have to try to figure out who is going to fill the role of a reliable dump-off guy. Roush makes sense, and his OU is only 8.5, but his role has been greatly reduced the last few weeks, and I just don’t know if Ben Johnson will suddenly trust him again due to an injury. Raymond’s role has also been reduced, but I think he’s the guy who sees an uptick in targets. 16.5 yards isn’t much. Raymond should be able to do that in just 1 or 2 catches, but he’s only gone over this total once in the last four weeks, and it was 18 yards. This is more a play that Raymond is on the field more and will see a couple more targets due to the Kmet injury.

BONUS: Jeffery Simmons 0.5 sacks or more +154

For the purposes of these articles, I only give straight 50-50 props and stopped dabbling in the plus-money waters a couple of years ago. But wanted to at least drop this one in as a bonus. I think Simmons plays at least 50% of the snaps tonight, and I just think big players like this always have that extra little bit of motivation to show up that first game in a new location. I go back to Khalil Mack’s first half against Green Bay in his debut. I think Simmons makes a couple of impact plays, so corralling San Darnold for a sack feels like a good wager to make.

item.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 9: Latest news, updates on Breece Hall, Jeremiyah Love, more players for fantasy football
item.description: We go over the NFL injury report going into Week 9, with player updates, news and fantasy football analysis.
item.content:encoded:
Week 9 is the official midway point of the 2026 NFL season. So by now you know what you have on your fantasy football roster. You also know who has been healthy the majority of the year and which players have missed time. It feels like the injury report is thinning out a bit as we get into the middle of the campaign. But as always, we're tracking all the latest news and updates for you, to help with those fantasy football lineups.

NFL Injury Report, Week 9

Quarterback

  • Lamar Jackson, BAL (thumb) — Headed for injured reserve

  • Tyler Huntley, BAL (toe) — Could miss extended time

Ravens QBs: Jackson left in the first half of Sunday's loss to the Bills. He needs surgery on his thumb and is headed for IR. He'll miss at least four games, if not the rest of the season. After Jackson exited, Huntley entered the game and also had to leave due to injury (turf toe), leaving Baltimore down to third-string rookie Joe Fagnano. As if things couldn't get worse, Fagnano got banged up Sunday as well.

It doesn't look like Huntley will be ready for Week 9 and the Ravens can't proceed with Fagnano as the starter. The team is expected to make a move for a QB before the trade deadline, which is next week. Whoever ends up starting for the Ravens will need to be evaluated for fantasy. We'll update you when we get word on who the QB is and go from there.

Running Back

  • Christian McCaffrey, SF (hamstring)

  • Jeremiyah Love, ARI (ankle)

  • Bam Knight, ARI (concussion)

  • Cam Skattebo, NYG (hamstring)

  • Breece Hall, NYJ (quad) — Expected to be back in Week 9

  • Kyle Monangai, CHI (toe/thumb)

  • David Montgomery, HOU (groin)

  • Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Could be activated off IR

  • TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness)

  • Brian Robinson Jr., ATL (hamstring)

  • Jadarian Price, SEA (chest) — Expected to be activated off IR

Hall: We thought the Jets were going to get back Hall in Week 8 against the Raiders. That wasn't the case and we got another solid game from Braelon Allen. At this point, even if Hall comes back, expect Allen to be involved given how well he's performed. Allen is the RB5 overall in half-PPR scoring from Weeks 5-8 with Hall sidelined. We'll need to get a look at how the split is in Week 9 if Hall is back. Plus, it's a tough draw against Kansas City's run defense. But better matchups loom, so don't be surprised if both Hall and Allen are viable RB2/3 options.

Cardinals RBs: Love aggravated his ankle injury in the comeback win over Dallas in OT on Sunday. Knight exited after a big hit and should land in concussion protocol. It'll be tough for Knight to clear in time for Week 9 against the Seahawks, but we'll see. Love has had so many issues with the ankle in his rookie season, it's hard to view him as a sure thing for this week. If both are out, Tyler Allgeier will be playable, but don't expect 33.6 fantasy points — or anywhere close to that — against Seattle's top defense.

McCaffrey: CMC comes off the bye navigating a mild hamstring strain. It doesn't feel like this will cause him to miss Week 9 against the Raiders. But we saw before San Francisco's bye that Kyle Shanahan feels comfortable giving the ball to rookie Kaelon Black. We could see more of Black on Sunday to help keep McCaffrey fresh.

Wide Receiver

  • Christian Watson, GB (ribs)

  • DeVonta Smith, PHI (hamstring)

  • Michael Wilson, ARI (ribs)

  • Mike Evans, SF (Achilles)

  • A.J. Brown, NE (ankle/knee)

  • Emeka Egbuka, TB (foot) — Could play in Week 9

  • Jordyn Tyson, NO (hamstring) — Could come off IR

  • Deebo Samuel Sr., SF (hamstring)

Watson: The Packers' lead receiver had a miraculous exit and return to TNF's win over the Panthers in Week 8. Watson finished with an 8-113-0 line on 10 targets, catching a few passes after coming back from the hospital. But Watson revealed he's dealing with a broken rib, which is less than ideal. He'll have ample time to rest before Week 9's matchup with the Patriots. Watson could play through the injury, but if he's active, he would be at risk of exiting the game early. If Watson ends up having to sit, Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams would likely see more targets. Matthew Golden would be elevated into WR1 territory as well.

Wilson: The Cardinals' receiver told reporters after Sunday's win over the Cowboys that he's dealing with broken ribs. It appears Wilson is going to play through the injury. He's a risky option in the flex in PPR formats going up against the Seahawks' stout defense in Week 9.

Egbuka: The Bucs wideout has missed the past two games, and Tampa's passing game sure could use him. The Bucs didn't complete a pass in Week 8's shutout win over the Falcons, instead opting to run the ball 56 times for 324 yards. That likely won't be the case in Chicago in Week 9. If Egbuka can get back, it's a decent matchup, though Tampa Bay ranks dead last in passing offense this season. Egbuka would be a risky flex in PPR at best.

Ferguson: The Cowboys lost Ferguson to a low-ankle sprain early in the game against Arizona. He didn't return and his status for Week 9 against the Colts could be up in the air. If Ferguson is out, this is still a passing game dominated by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Ryan Flournoy has stepped up as a solid WR3 as well. Brevyn Ford-Spann played 88% of the snaps in Week 8 and had four catches on five targets for 31 yards. In deeper formats, Ford-Spann isn't a bad streamer. He could see garbage-time looks if the Cowboys run away against a struggling Indy team.

item.title: Arizona Cardinals Daily Links: Cards earn ‘B’ in comeback win over Cowboys
item.description: The Cardinals came back from double-digits to beat the Cowboys on the road in Dallas.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals showed an immense amount of grit and emotional fortitude in their comeback win over the Cowboys, which included a quarterback switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew.

Mike LaFleur earned his third win of his head-coaching career and it came in dramatic fashion. Kicker Chad Ryland missed an extra point attempt that would have won it in regulation, but he came back to drill the game-winner in overtime.

For their efforts, CBS Sports’ John Breech gave the Cardinals a “B” grade. Here’s what he had to say:

‘‘The Cardinals might have just found themselves a new starting QB. With the offense going nowhere, Mike LaFleur decided to bench Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter in favor of Gardner Minshew, and that gamble paid off big time. Minshew entered the game and immediately proceeded to have one of the best fourth quarters of any QB this season: He threw for 166 yards and three touchdowns, including a game-tying 13-yard score to Michael Wilson with just six seconds left in regulation. The Cardinals have plenty of weapons on offense; they just need a QB who can utilize them, and it’s possible that Minshew might be that guy. Minshew was so good that it wouldn’t be surprising if the Cardinals decided to start taking offers for Brissett before the trade deadline.”

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs is the NFL MVP, so far
item.description: Modern analytics and traditional box score statistics prove Jahmyr Gibbs belongs in the NFL MVP conversation.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 will be a memorable one for the 2026 season. It moved the Lions into a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North, keeping them at a perfect 2-0 in all-important divisional games. It allowed the 1972 Miami Dolphins to pop the cork on their celebratory champagne as the league’s only undefeated team. And it also set the stage for the NFL to have its first running back since 2012 to claim the league’s MVP award.

Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, and if he’s going to keep doing what he’s been doing over these first couple of months, he should end up being the MVP.

If you’re over the age of 40, congratulations, you’ve been gifted—blessed—the unique opportunity to see two of the best running backs in NFL history. I’ve been done with tiptoeing around the comparisons to Barry Sanders—he’s doing stuff like this on a weekly basis:

But it’s not just the highlight plays that paint him as the heir apparent to Sanders; you see it in the numbers, too. Gibbs sports the fourth-best success rate among running backs at 48.4% across 157 carries, but he also has the most stuffed runs—rushes that result in gains of zero or negative yardage—in the NFL (33) and ranks 38th among 46 qualifying running backs in stuffed rate (21.0%) according to SumerStats. Through the lens of modern analytics, it doesn’t get much more Sanders-esque than that.

Given the sheer volume of his workload, his success rate becomes that much more impressive among his peers. The three running backs with higher success rates are Blake Corum (75 rushing attempts), Christian McCaffrey (84), and Jaylen Warren (119). The preseason comments about Gibbs becoming the bell-cow running back for Detroit couldn’t have been more prescient, and right now, he’s the frontrunner for Best in Show.

Gibbs is averaging the most yards from scrimmage among running backs (149.9 yards), and the next closest player—Kenneth Walker—is over 20 yards off pace. He leads the league in missed tackles forced (51) in just seven games, according to Pro Football Focus. Last year’s leader in missed tackles forced was Bijan Robinson at 86. Gibbs’ current pace of 121 would be the highest recorded figure in PFF’s stat tracking history. He has the most runs of 10+ yards (27) and is currently seventh in yards after contact per attempt (3.56)—second in total yards after contact (559) according to SumerStats.

But the real measure for MVP voting will rely on the traditional box score statistics, and Gibbs is on track to hit all the benchmarks to put together a special season worthy of MVP consideration. He’s averaging over 110 rushing yards per game and on pace for nearly 1,900 rushing yards, which really helps put 2,000 yards in perspective given how incredible Gibbs has been. He’s averaging over a touchdown per game (1.4) and on pace for 24 total touchdowns—the highest mark since LaDainian Tomlinson set the single-season record 20 years ago with 31 en route to his MVP award. If it’s not rewriting the history books like LT in 2006, it takes absurd numbers plus a narrative for a running back to win the award. Adrian Peterson’s 2012 season, where he carried a deeply flawed Vikings offense to the playoffs by rushing for 2,097 yards, was the last time those stars aligned.

What’s unique about Gibbs’ chance at becoming the first running back to win the award in over a decade is the relative lack of standouts at the quarterback position through eight weeks. Statistically speaking, Joe Burrow is putting together the numbers—first in completion percentage (73%), touchdown passes (20), and passing yards per game (302.1)—but if the Bengals can’t beat out the Pittsburgh Steelers for the AFC North, and if their defense keeps them out of the playoffs for another season, would voters crown him the league’s MVP? Trevor Lawrence’s impressive start to the season includes 17 touchdown passes to just four interceptions, and he leads the NFL in passer rating, so maybe there’s something there if he keeps on pace. If Josh Allen wins the award for his second time in three seasons because he has a bunch of one-yard rushing touchdowns, so be it; at least we’ll know a non-QB will never have a chance to win the league’s MVP moving forward.

The NFL has spent the last decade-plus morphing into a pass-heavy league where running backs are sold as replaceable, interchangeable pieces to an offense. Without David Montgomery sharing the backfield, Gibbs is tearing down that narrative. He’s delivering game-breaking efficiency behind an offensive line that’s been good, but not great. While critics might point out that he plays in one of the league’s most potent offenses, anyone watching Detroit each Sunday knows Gibbs is the single biggest key to their success.

If the MVP award is truly meant for the player who dictates defenses, transforms and elevates an entire offense, and shoulders great expectations for contender week in and week out, then the 2026 race shouldn’t default to the coronation of just another quarterback—it should belong to the league’s most explosive and irreplaceable player.

item.title: Jason Witten reportedly becomes the offensive play-caller at Oklahoma
item.description: If, as some believe, former Cowboys tight end Jason Witten is destined to eventually become the head coach of America's team, he's taking the next step in his coaching career with Oklahoma's team.
item.content:encoded:
If, as some believe, former Cowboys tight end Jason Witten is destined to eventually become the head coach of America's team, he's taking the next step in his coaching career with Oklahoma's team.

Via SoonerScoop.com, Witten will become the offensive play-caller at the University of Oklahoma, following the in-season firing of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle.

Witten has been serving as the Sooners' tight ends coach. He had been a high-school coach since 2021.

The 44-year-old Witten initially retired after 15 seasons with the Cowboys, worked on Monday Night Football for a season, and then returned to the NFL for 2019 (with the Cowboys) and 2020 (with the Raiders). He's in his first year as a college coach.

Whether he eventually works for the Cowboys as an assistant coach or is eventually hired to run the whole show, there's a sense that Witten will inevitably be on the Dallas staff.

item.title: After scary injury to Jack Campbell, Lions get emotional win over Vikings: 'It was all about Jack'
item.description: Detroit linebacker Jack Campbell was resting and expected to spend the night in the hospital for testing and monitoring after sustaining a neck injury in the Lions' game against the Minnesota Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was resting and expected to spend the night in the hospital for testing and monitoring after sustaining a scary neck injury, the team announced soon after its 19-15 victory against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday afternoon.

Campbell, a fourth-year player who made his first Pro Bowl last season, was lying face down and motionless on the field after tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter.

Players were emotional as they knelt on the field, and the crowd watched in concerned silence as medical staff tended to the injured player for around 10 minutes, before strapping him to a backboard and carting him off the field. Campbell is said to have been breathing and alert when he was taken to the hospital.

Read more:Swanson: Chargers’ lost season really could become the NFL’s first 0-17 humiliation

“Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family,” Lions coach Dan Campbelltold reporters after the game. “He’s being taken care of. We don’t have any new information. We’ll keep you updated as this goes, but we’re thinking about him.”

In the locker room, the coach was fired up as he congratulated his players on a gritty victory over an NFC North rival that had entered the game undefeated. He quickly became emotional when the topic turned to their injured teammate.

Together pic.twitter.com/1AIUMwGF7w

— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 2, 2026

“I do not have any more information on Jack,” he said. “We don’t know anything else at this point. So here’s what I want to do, man. We’re gonna take a knee and I want to pray for Jack, OK? And let’s keep him in our thoughts and prayers, man.”

Jack Campbell was injured on the first play of the fourth quarter, with the Lions clinging to a 12-7 lead. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray completed a 10-yard pass to Hockenson on the play, with the tackle by Campbell and teammate Jimmy Rolder setting up fourth down and 5 yards to go for Minnesota. Rolder also suffered a hamstring injury on the play and did not return to the game.

Read more:Sean McVay's unusual kicker experiment leaves Rams with little margin for error

Before play resumed, Detroit edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson gathered the defense and delivered a few heartfelt words.

An emotional @aidanhutch97 being a leader for the @Lions defense after Jack Campbell was carted off. pic.twitter.com/ssy0VQVlNi

— FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026

Then he and his teammates went back to work, with Hutchinson applying pressure on Murray and Lions cornerback D.J. Reed knocking the ball away from intended receiver Jordan Anderson for an incomplete pass and a turnover on downs.

“I was filled with a lot of emotions,” Hutchinson told reporters after the game. “We were more united than we had ever been before that play. It’s a weird dynamic, between football being a game, and then snap out of it to seeing a dude being carted off, and then right back in it. Riding that roller coaster, it’s a little foreign, for sure.”

Immediately after returning to the sideline, Detroit’s defensive players gathered in a circle.

The Lions defense takes a moment after Jack Campbell was carted off. @ErinAndrews has more. pic.twitter.com/uvy9PfrITI

— FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026

“In those type of moments, you forget football,” Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes told reporters after the game. “It’s about the person. Football was the last thing on my mind when that happened. It was all about Jack.”

Thursday Night Football continues to draw larger audiences, generally. Specifically, there will be some peaks and valleys.

item.title: Jaguars Winners and Losers From Week 8: Jags Dominate Lifeless Colts
item.description: Winners are all around after Jacksonville’s thrashing of the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
As we have said in this column all year: sometimes you just need to beat the brakes off a bad team. The Jacksonville Jaguars did just that on Sunday, winning 42-7 over the hapless and directionless Indianapolis Colts. 

Sunday’s box score was just about as good as it could possibly get with Trevor Lawrence throwing effectively and with command. Bhayshul Tuten played incredibly well and even Brian Thomas Jr. caught a ball. Defensively, the Jags had four sacks with one even coming from Travon Walker. The Colts suck but it still was a needed divisional win to keep the Jaguars atop the AFC South and in the hunt for a top overall AFC seed.

Jacksonville even got better news later in the day when Baltimore Ravens’ quarterback Lamar Jackson hit injured reserve before Thursday night’s game in Baltimore. Unfortunately for Jacksonville, the injury bug bit the team hard Sunday with DaVon Hamilton being the big name hurt. Hamilton was carted off the field and it has been reported he tore his quad and is done for the year.

But such is life in the National Football League. For now, it’s time for a Victory Monday celebration.

WINNERS

Bhayshul Tuten

The Jags made an incredible decision when they decided to give the running back room keys to Tuten. It has paid off in a huge way with almost inarguably Tuten’s best game coming Sunday against the Colts.

The second-year running back led the team in both receiving (two catches for 55 yards and one score) and rushing (16 carries for 104 yards and one score). He scored twice in one game for the second time in two consecutive tries. His 159 total yards were the most by a Jag since 2023.

Tuten’s hard, downhill running style gives the Jags an extremely helpful punisher on offense that most teams simply are not prepared for. When Tuten is tooting along, the Jags are a nasty offense that can score with the best of them. 

Nate Boerkircher

The conversation on Nate Boerkircher has been very fun. No, he does not get 20 targets a game but he certainly makes the most of them when he does.

The rookie second-rounder caught just one pass on Sunday, but he took it for 31 yards and a score. Like Tuten, he has touchdowns now in back-to-back games after going scoreless for the first five games of his career.

Boerkircher caught his pass for Lawrence – who did an incredible job to evade pressure – and found himself wide open. It wasn’t a one-handed leap like last week, but the rook has caught all five of his targets in his last three games.

The Defensive Line

For weeks, or even years at this point, we have all been calling for sacks from this defensive line. That all fixed itself on Sunday.

Jacksonville left its game against the Colts with four sacks. Foye Oluokun, Travon Walker and randomly rookie safety Jalen Huskey all had full sacks. Josh Hines-Allen and Arik Armstead were both credited with .5 each. You would have to go all the way back to the opener when the Jags had that many sacks in a game when they had five against the Browns.

In terms of PFF grades, three Jags defensive linemen were among the top-five graded players. It got so bad for the Colts that even Rayuan Lane (who had a nice game by the way) was getting pressures. Finally, a full-circle game from that defensive line unit.

As an aside, with Hamilton’s injury, this probably forces the hand of the Jags to make a play for a run-stopping defensive lineman. That trade could very even include sending Brian Thomas Jr. somewhere else. Maybe this is all addition by subtraction in the end.

Travis Hunter

Sunday was not a “Travis Hunter game” but he just simply rocks as a Jaguar. He looks cool in the rivalries and is an asset on both sides of the ball. He truly is a force multiplier because offenses have to be worried about throwing near him and defenses have to worry about his quick shift speed as a receiver. Yeah, it took a little for it all to shake out in terms of usage, but it is all working well now.

Al’s Pizza

Courtesy of two Daniel Jones picks to Lane and Branson Combs (never thought I’d type those names together) Jaguars fans can get 50% Al’s Pizza with the code PIZZAPICKOFF. What’s better than some pizza and the knowledge that at least two AFC South teams are utterly horrible?

LOSERS

Injuries

That Hamilton injury is going to be an issue. No telling how big or when, but it’s going to change some things. And he was not alone. Walker got banged up and so did guard Ezra Cleveland. No injury is worse than seeing Hamilton carted off the field Sunday morning after how well he has been playing, though. Christian Barmore is a name that comes to mind to replace Hamilton, but we will have to see. That victory on Sunday could have been that much better if the Jags were to come out of it healthy. 

The Rest of the NFL

There are some real bad teams in the NFL. The Jacksonville Jaguars aren’t one of them.

Across the league, the Bucs won a game without completing a pass. The Titans took the Bengals to overtime. The Cowboys lost again. The Chargers lost AGAIN. The Vikings still can’t score on offense and the Eagles might just quit playing football altogether. A decent bit has been said about how cupcake the schedule ahead is for Jacksonville, but so what? We can’t help that we are good when everyone else outside of like three seems seemingly suck. What a great time to be a fan of the Jaguars.

Give us your thoughts on Sunday’s game and some names of who you might want to see the Jags acquire to replace Hamilton. And we will see you right back here on a short week as the Jags look to keep the good vibes going against Baltimore on Thursday.

item.title: Smyth in contention as Saints evaluate kicker slot
item.description: Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Dan Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns.
item.content:encoded:
Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Daniel Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns.

Carlson has been the Saints' first-choice kicker this season, but the 31-year-old has struggled for consistency.

Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in County Down, made his NFL debut last season but returned to the practice roster after the Saints elected to bring in Carlson for the start of the current campaign.

However, Carlson's form has opened the door for Smyth to potentially return to the playing roster. Moore said both he and his coaching staff will "evaluate the field goal situation and opportunities".

Moore said that the Saints had not brought any additional kickers into their squad, which leaves Smyth and Carlson in contention to start against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

"That's something we'll have to work through and discuss to find the best solution for Sunday," said Moore.

"We'll see how it goes. We'll have some kicking sessions throughout this week and we'll see where we are at."

Former Gaelic footballer Smyth made 12 of 16 field goals and was successful on each of his 13 extra point attempts as a starter last season, after his historic NFL debut last November.

He had a mixed pre-season and Carlson was selected to be the Saints' first choice after a kicking competition ahead of the NFL season.

But Carlson has a success rate of 66% this season from 12 field goal attempts and his only perfect game with the boot came in September, when he landed three kicks against the Baltimore Ravens.

He has made 16 of his 18 extra point attempts as the Saints have just two wins from seven games this season.

item.title: Ranking Jonathan Taylor's best fits amid trade rumors surrounding Colts RB
item.description: The Colts may trade Jonathan Taylor ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Here's a look at which potential suitors would be the best fit for the star RB.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts began their fire sale when they traded longtime stalwart guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and dealt defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on the same day.

The Colts' teardown is expected to continue after the team suffered a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a Week 8 game where they didn't look remotely competitive.

Naturally, rumors have started swirling about the potential availability of their star running back, Jonathan Taylor. Reports indicate that the team is open to trading the 27-year-old, and he would have no shortage of suitors if made available before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

But which suitors would provide the best landing spots for Taylor? Several contenders stand out from the pack, and the team currently sporting the NFL's best record may ultimately be the best fit for him.

Here's a ranking of the top five fits for Taylor should the Colts trade him ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.

1. Minnesota Vikings

The Vikings are sitting at 6-1, but they are still in desperate need of an offensive identity. They are averaging just 20 points per game this season – good for sixth-fewest in the league – and have only 12 offensive touchdowns to their name.

Among Minnesota's issues this season are that the team's Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason-led running game ranks 27th in rushing EPA per play this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Jones had a nice stretch as the team's lead back, but the 31-year-old is battling a nagging knee injury, so it may be hard for him to remain productive as the Vikings enter a more difficult stretch of their schedule.

Taylor would be an instant upgrade over the solid-but-uninspiring duo of Jones and Mason thanks to his three-down abilities. He would allow Kevin O'Connell to lean on the running game as the engine that drives his offense, and having a true workhorse would allow Minnesota to marry a ground-dominant, possession-based offense with their elite, attacking-style Brian Flores defense.

If Taylor could just help shape the Vikings into an average offense, it would go a long way toward establishing them as a legitimate NFC contender.

2. Denver Broncos

The Broncos are a very close No. 2 option behind the Vikings as a top fit for Taylor's services. The emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman, who racked up 104 yards and a touchdown on 15 touches in Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs, gives them a bit more flexibility in trade talks than the Vikings, but there's still little doubt that adding Taylor to Denver's offense would provide the team a big boost.

As good as Coleman has looked, the remainder of Denver's running back room has endured its share of issues. J.K. Dobbins' negative-1.1 rushing yards over expected per attempt ranks third-worst among qualified running backs this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats, while RJ Harvey is on IR with a knee injury and is looking more like a pass-catching back than a between the tackles option.

Adding Taylor would give the Broncos certainty at the running back position and create a dynamic, one-two punch with Coleman. Taylor could play a majority of the downs with Coleman serving as a change-of-pace option and Dobbins, Harvey and Tyler Badie rounding out a running back depth chart that would be described as elite.

Having a strong, multi-faceted running game would also go a long way toward supporting Bo Nix, who has had an up-and-down season thus far in 2026. Giving him elite-level rushing support and allowing him to function as more of a game manager could ultimately be the formula the Broncos need to make a Super Bowl run this season.

3. Seattle Seahawks

To say the Seahawks' plans at running back have gone awry would be an understatement. They replaced Kenneth Walker III with first-round rookie Jadarian Price after losing the Super Bowl 60 MVP in free agency, but Price struggled with fumbles before suffering a chest injury that landed him on IR.

With Zach Charbonnet also out of action while recovering from a torn ACL, the Seahawks have relied on Emanuel Wilson to carry them. The power back has performed admirably, but he is still entering his Week 8 "Monday Night Football" contest averaging just 3.6 yards per carry.

Both Charbonnet and Price are expected back in Week 8, so perhaps if the running back rotation looks good against the Bears, it will quell concerns about the Seahawks needing to add a top-tier running back. But if not, John Schneider could look to swing a second trade with the Colts after acquiring Nelson to improve the team's interior offensive line.

Nelson is one of the NFL's best run blockers, so Seattle has all the makings of a talented rushing attack. Taylor would take that to the next level, and the Seahawks should be very interested in adding another top-tier playmaker to an offense that has thus far been carried by Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

4. New York Giants

Cam Skattebo had the best game of his professional career in Week 7 against the Houston Texans, racking up 124 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. For that reason, the Giants don't necessarily need to trade for a running back ahead of the deadline.

Even so, Skattebo was on shaky footing ahead of his breakout game. He was effectively benched the previous week after fumble issues, playing six offensive snaps and getting zero touches, so John Harbaugh might like to have another high-end option for his offense in case those issues flare up again.

Having Taylor and Skattebo together would immediately create one of the most fearsome two-man running back attacks in the league. It would also go a long way toward replenishing a Giants depth chart that has been thinned by an injury to Tyrone Tracy Jr. and the release of Najee Harris.

Add in that the Giants have a relatively clear path toward winning the NFC East and swinging a trade for a piece like Taylor, who fits the timeline of New York's window for contention since he is under contract through 2028, could prove sensible.

5. New England Patriots

I know, I know. The Patriots probably have bigger needs to target than running back ahead of the trade deadline. They could use another talented wide receiver as A.J. Brown continues to deal with injury issues, and could also stand to add depth to their edge rush, which is currently just three deep.

Still, New England could use an upgrade at the running back position. Rhamondre Stevenson has been a solid starter, but his 3.8 yards per carry average leaves a bit to be desired. Meanwhile, TreVeyon Henderson has struggled to stay on the field and hasn't often shown off the speed that was supposed to make him a dynamic threat at running back this season.

Mike Vrabel is familiar with Taylor, having coached against him often during his time with the Tennessee Titans. Vrabel could see the benefit of adding Taylor and relegating Stevenson and Henderson to situational roles for which they may be better suited.

Having elite depth at running back could help the Patriots offset their injury issues at receiver, where Brown has missed five games and Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are both on IR.

item.title: Raiders rally with resurgent 2nd half to ground Jets 38-33 in road win
item.description: Las Vegas offense and defense come to life helping team outscore New York 24-10 to snap four-game losing skid
item.content:encoded:
A tale of two halves.

It’s a hackneyed description of sporting events in general, however, what occurred within the confines of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey between the visiting Las Vegas Raiders and the host New York Jets epitomized that classic phrase.

Gang Green came out like gangbusters at home going 5-for-5 on each of its first-half offensive possessions to build a 23-14 advantage at halftime. And after Braelon Allen’s hard-charging 21-yard gallop in the third quarter, the Jets went an impeccable 6-for-6 with points scored after each of those drives orchestrated by offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterback (and former Raider) Geno Smith.

The Silver & Black, meanwhile, produced just 103 yards on offense and a single touchdown — a ridiculous one-handed grab by tight end Brock Bowers — while reserve running back and dynamic kick return man Dylan Laube made a house call on a 95-yard kickoff return (the first of the 2026 NFL season, by the way) and only possessed the ball for 10:43 compared to the Jets 19:17 time of possession.

But that Allen breakaway-touchdown was the last end zone visit for the Jets. The Raiders put forth an exhibition in complementary football in the second half going 3-for-3 on their offensive possessions to outscore New York 24-10 as the J-E-T-S, L-O-S-T a game in which they dominated in the first half.

The Silver & Black’s display of resurgence and resilience (which had been lacking in the four-consecutive losses) produced a rally and a 38-33 Las Vegas win to snap the four-game slide and get the team back to .500 at 4-4 overall.

“I thought halftime-wise, our guys (said), ‘We’re not happy,’” Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said after the game. “We made some adjustments and the guys just played harder. Our guys kept battling.”

With Las Vegas opening up the third quarter with a methodical 10-play, 65-yard drive that culminated in Bowers’ second touchdown (two-yard variety), Rob Leonard’s much-maligned defense held its own against Reich, Smith, and Co. in the second stanza limiting the Jets offense to two punts, a field goal, and ending the game with an interception. That just showcases the dramatic 180-degree turn the two teams did after trading touchdowns at the onset of the third quarter.

“It’s just about taking a stand,” Raiders edge rusher Crosby said. “At some point it really comes down to winning your one-on-one’s and outworking the man in front of you. That’s what I felt like we did. We came out with an attitude in the second half and I feel like we played a lot better collectively.”

With the defense no longer rolling out the carpet in red zone, Kubiak and his offense led by veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins went to work besting head coach Aaron Glenn’s Jets defense. Another 10-play, 65-yard drive ended with Cousins’ one-yard QB sneak to cut the deficit to 30-28 late in the third quarter. Las Vegas’ ensuing drive after a New York punt was a nine-play, 84-yard end zone visit that featured a screen pass to running back Ashton Jeanty who fell after the catch but got up untouched for a 45-yard gain. That helped set up the Cousins-to-Nailor connection for a touchdown (the tweet above) to generate a 35-30 lead for the Raiders.

The two teams traded field goals late in the fourth (which became the eventual final score) and Las Vegas safety Jeremy Chinn made up for a 15-yard penalty unnecessary roughness on his hit on Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson with a game-ending, toe-tap interception of Smith’s last-gasp end zone heave.

There’s plenty of areas of opportunity for the Raiders — namely beating a good team rather than dropping bad teams — but snapping the skid with a road win is a good sign nonetheless.

Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Laube sprinted past the Jets special teams on his kick return touchdown:

—Cousins is simply thriving in his reunion with Kubiak as he threw three touchdowns and totaled 297 yards on 19 of 26 passing. He was sacked once but continues to be an accurate ball distributor in Kubiak’s Raiders offense. The 38-year-old quarterback even had a unique celebration on his touchdown plunge.

—Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. paced the ground game with 25 carries for 83 yards (3.3 yards per carry average) and a long of 15. He out-touched his much higher drafted teammate Jeanty (two carries for nine yards). Kubiak said after the game the call to put the ball in Washington’s hands was his and Jeanty remains a “big part” of the Raiders offense.

—Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer continue to be active targets as the former finished with seven receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns while the latter had five catches for 53 yards. Jeanty was sandwiched between the two hauling in three passes for 64 yards.

—Middle linebacker Nakobe Dean paced the Raiders defense with 12 total tackles. Chinn was second with 10 total stops. Pass-rush wise, Crosby racked up a sack as did nose tackle Tim Keenan III. Speaking of Keenan, he’s every bit of his listed 6-foot-2 and 327-pound frame — if not even bigger than that.

—Smith was letting it fly in the first half showcasing that he still can throw a nice deep ball. He did have bouts of inaccuracy but finished 20 of 32 for 290 yards with two touchdowns and a pick. He was sacked twice. His favorite targets — wide receivers Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson — were productive with the former having seven catches for 142 yards and a score and the latter with six grabs for 83 yards.

—Once Raiders rookies Treydan Stukes gets the NFL speed and timing down, the pass breakups he had against the Jets can turn into takeaways (interceptions). He jumped too early on Smith’s end zone pass to rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq on New York’s opening drive and again on Mitchell’s deep catch (tweet above). Ditto for rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses who also jumped too early on a would-be pick of Smith in the fourth quarter.

Quotes of Note

“The Silver & Black (were) out. We heard them, they were loud. They supported us pregame, all during the game and especially in that fourth quarter. That was really special, very grateful for our fans. Our players (were) very resilient, played four quarters of football. It wasn’t all pretty, but it’s not always going to be pretty. It’’s finding a way to win.”

—Las Vegas Raider head coach Klint Kubiak on the well-traveled Raider Nation fan base who were vocal in MetLife Stadium

“I’ve always tried to not ride the roller coaster. But that also means when things are going well, I’m a little more steady. You’ve just got to believe that if you keep playing, there’s a good chance you’ll be there in the fourth quarter.”

—Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on the second-half explosion compared to getting stonewalled in the fist half

Up Next

The Raiders draw quite the challenge this coming Sunday with the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers. The Niners will head to the desert for the Week 9 matchup inside Allegiant Stadium and come off a bye week. San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan is no stranger to Kubiak (the younger and elder, Klint’s father Gary) and is eager to get his NFC West-leading team back in the win column after being stunned by the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 29-20.

item.title: The potentially good O-linemen the Seattle Seahawks lost in pursuit of the great
item.description: The Seahawks offensive line has been baptized in competition ever since Mike Macdonald came to town.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a saying: “Sometimes you have to say no to the good to get the great.” Seattle has aggressively taken on that mindset to wash the offensive line with talent over the last few years.

It was a glorious thing to watch Seattle subvert the storyline, flipping it on its head for the world to see on SNF. All season it’s been: “The Seahawks are missing Kenneth Walker III, that’s why they haven’t looked the same!” A dash of: “they messed up by letting Ken walk.” Seattle shut down a prolific back, and themselves rushed for over 150 as a team in a bounce back performance at Lumen, slamming the door on all the narratives.

Anthony Bradford came back from injury, and played well, contributing to that rushing performance. Even so, the 2026 Seattle Seahawks are not getting complacent, choosing, rather, to run it forward.

Quenton Nelson is an undeniable game changer and talent. His reputation alone may make defensive squads feel the pressure to line up to respect the run a little more. Seattle got it done to their standard of a ground game against KC… but they didn’t want to take any more chances of the offense devolving again, especially with a rematch against SF, and a double feature on tap against a still dangerous Rams team.

Angling to get better at all positions led to the loss of Bryce Cabeldue to the Raiders.

Christian Haynes is the latest victim of Seattle’s transformation of the blocking unit.

Former Seahawks offensive lineman Ray Roberts appeared on the Wyman & Bob radio show, and said: “Someone had to go, and you still don’t know what you have in Beau Stephens. You may have a better idea of what you have in Christian Haynes. I don’t think that Christian ever fit the mold that they were looking for. I can remember earlier, like his rookie year, I think Coach Macdonald made the comment that like, he can get it done, but it doesn’t look the way you want it to look getting it done. So, he’s a little bit, kind of awkward in his approach and everything. Also, they kind of give the dudes about three years around here, to kind of figure out whether you have staying power, or you don’t.

Having all that been said, it’s still weird to see him in Dolphins colors already.

Matt Hasselbeck also appeared on Wyman & Bob and fleshed out developmental advantages to having Nelson on the squad. He explained that “the young guys on this roster are going to be better for having been his teammate, for having seen his process, seen how he works, seen how he prepares and studies. The most famous #8 in Hawks history went on to drop a gem of a saying: “more is caught than taught.”

Quenton Nelson, for his part, sounds ready to go to battle for Seattle: “It’s great to have all those memories and years spent in Indy, but, like I said: I’m excited for this.” The future gold jacket player went on to say, “I think I can do any kind of scheme.”

Cooper Kupp said that Nelson has, “seen a lot of football.” This falls in line with the Seahawks’ farm system, or, what I saw Seaside Joe calling, “the buddy system.”

Both Jeff Saturday, as well as Nelson’s replacement in Indianapolis, 4th-Round rookie, Jalen Farmer have independently mentioned how Q. has promised to stay in the young gun’s ear, even despite now being on a new team. That may not hold for the whole year, but it shows his dedication and intention as a teammate.

That’s what great players do.

How should we feel about Anthony Bradford? He’s come a long way: from public enemy #1 on offense, at times, to possibly even moving into the realm of good. Seattle’s has sights set on being more than good.

Coach Macdonald on the messaging to Bradford: “It’s not an easy situation. I thought Anthony played really good football for us, and he has. He’s earned a significant role in our team, a starting level role. It’s one of those through, not around type of things with A.B. that is not easy. There’s really no way to sugarcoat it.”

Seahawks GM, John Schneider was catching heat for a while for calling offensive guards “overpaid and over-drafted”, even after the seeming mistakes of getting rid of Max Unger and letting Damien Lewis walk to become a premier OG in Carolina.

Since then, he has been aggressive in reshaping this offensive line. Q. Nelson may be the finishing touch on that agenda. The pain of watching Laken Tomlinson let pressure through may have directly led to Grey Zable being drafted.

How high can this line climb? Will it be the best in recent Seattle memory? Can it get this run game on track and on a dominant pace? All possible, but time will tell.

item.title: Hammond isn't giving up on Bears making a move to Indiana
item.description: The Bears are where we thought they were.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears are where we thought they were. And it appears they’ll be staying.

But Indiana isn't giving up just yet. Hammond Mayor Thomas McDermott Jr. believes the Bears will still cross the border.

At times, however, he wonders what will happen.

“There’s some days when you talk to me and ask, ‘Mayor, are the Bears coming,’ and I’ll be 100% positive and there’s some days that I’m not as positive, OK?" McDermott said Friday, via Doug Ross of the Post-Tribune. "And that’s because it’s changing every second.”

The one constant throughout the change is the perception that Hammond is simply a bluff for the Bears to get a deal done in Illinois.

“I think the Bears are dead serious, but what if they are playing us?" McDermott said. "What are you supposed to do?”

Hammond remains in a nothing-to-lose posture. It's not as if they're talking to two NFL teams and could potentially miss out on one by focusing on the other. It's the Bears or nothing.

Obviously, there's an investment of time and money that Hammond has made for something that could be a waste of both. What should Hammond do? Frankly, it should issue an ultimatum to the Bears.

Get it done or get lost. Break ground or get bent.

Hammond has allowed itself to become the leverage for the Bears to build a new stadium in Illinois. To those on the outside, it's obvious. To those calling the shots in Hammond, they've become sufficiently smitten by the possibility of getting the Bears that they have suspended disbelief.

To the obvious benefit of the Bears.

In the end, what will Hammond get? A fruit basket? A heartfelt "thank you"?

Either way, Hammond won't be getting an NFL team in an NFL stadium. Unless and until all options in Illinois evaporate and the Bears sign the paperwork and at least 24 NFL teams authorize the relocation and the shovels are buried in Hammond soil.

For now, Hammond should use those shovels in an effort to clear away any and all BS and force the Bears to commit.

item.title: The Jets aren’t good enough to overcome the mistakes they made against the Raiders
item.description: I have said it before. I will say it again. There are different types of bad teams in the NFL. For much of 2025, particularly at the end of the season with Brady Cook at quarterback, the Jets were a comedically mismatched bad team. They didn’t have the talent or the coaching necessary to be […]
item.content:encoded:
I have said it before. I will say it again.

There are different types of bad teams in the NFL.

For much of 2025, particularly at the end of the season with Brady Cook at quarterback, the Jets were a comedically mismatched bad team. They didn’t have the talent or the coaching necessary to be competitive with practically any of the other 31 teams.

In 2026 the Jets are also a bad team, but they are a different type of bad.

The talent level is better. Of course, that isn’t saying much. The Jets could be putting practically any sort of roster on the field and still be much better than what we saw at the end of last season.

The 2026 Jets still rank fairly low on talent relative to the rest of the league. That is particularly true on defense. I’m not sure many of the players who took the field in yesterday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders would see much playing time on a Super Bowl caliber defense. Even most of those who would make the cut almost certainly would have smaller roles than they have with the Jets.

There are any number of reasons the Jets are so low on talent on the defensive side of the ball. Teams do have to prioritize which areas they want to improve first in a rebuild, and the Jets have sunk many resources into their offense. There also have been a number of personnel miscalculations, particularly in free agency in 2026. I would also argue that the way the defense was built shows fundamental flaws. The pass rush seems entirely structured around one player, David Bailey, a developing rookie. We have seen the sort of up and down season we might expect from a rookie. When said rookie is out of the lineup, it makes things even more challenging, impossible even.

Things look brighter on offense where the Jets do have a number of young players showing real talent, but on the whole it would be fair to state that this remains a roster closer to the bottom than the top.

Teams like I just described can still win in the NFL. It requires them to be opportunistic. They need to find ways to equalize games. Being efficient in the red zone on offense and stingy in the red zone on defense is important. Ditto to protecting the ball and forcing turnovers. Playing top notch special teams also helps a lot. And through these things and more, quality coaching has a way of making up the gap.

Unfortunately, the Jets are poor in most of the aspects I just mentioned. Avoiding turnovers is really the only thing they are doing well at that point.

These flaws all manifested themselves in the team’s 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

Teams like the Jets just don’t have a margin for error, even against an opponent like the Raiders.

Most of the attention will rightly be given to a putrid defensive performance. There isn’t anything you can say to sugarcoat a game like that defensively. The Jets’ lack of defensive talent showed, but it wasn’t just that. Even basics of defense were a struggle. It seemed like on a number of occasions they lost track of Brock Bowers, which you just can’t do considering how important he is to the Raiders offense. And for a third straight week, the unit allowed the opponent to grind out the clock with a time consuming drive late in the fourth quarter.

This was a team loss, though.

A special teams unit that was the league’s best in a dismal 2025 has completely regressed. Week 8 was another ugly day for Chris Banjo and his group as they allowed a kickoff return touchdown.

On offense the day was a bright spot for the most part. The Jets put a season high 33 points on the board. Still, they left points on the field, settling for a field goal four times in the red zone. This included three stalled drives in the first half.

There were stretches where the Jets might have been able to seize control of the game had they made plays. The three first half red zone drives ending in field goals produced 9 points instead of 21. The touchdown gave the Raiders 7. Adding even some of those lost 19 points could have taken a 23-14 halftime lead into a territory where the Jets were in total control of the game.

Geno Smith misfired on two would be touchdown passes to Garrett Wilson in the first quarter. In the context of what turned into a superb day for Smith throwing the ball, I think we can give the quarterback some grace.

A drive that stalled before halftime, though, is tougher to defend. That drive stalled just before and after the two minute warning as Frank Reich called seven consecutive runs. It felt like Reich was prioritizing running out the clock so the Raiders couldn’t get the ball at the expense of scoring an important touchdown. Given how publicized the cartoonish point differential the Aaron Glenn Jets in the last two minutes of the first half has been over the last two weeks, it almost seemed like the Jets coaching staff was prioritizing not giving the Raiders a chance to score and make that differential worse over winning the game.

As I have mentioned in this space before, the best two minute drills find the right balance between maximizing points and leaving as little time as possible on the clock for the other team. Of the two, maximizing points should be the higher priority.

The Jets can win games, but they just aren’t good enough to overcome their inability to do the little things. That goes for their players and their coaches. And because these mistakes are made over and over, it seems increasingly likely the Jets will have a lot of new players and new coaches sooner rather than later.

item.title: Sunday Aftermath: Lamar Jackson's latest injury, Jonah Coleman's emergence, and more
item.description: Breaking down all of the NFL's biggest Week 8 storylines, including Lamar Jackson's thumb injury.
item.content:encoded:
Some injuries have takeaways. Others have ramifications. Such is the case with Lamar Jackson and his thumb. For the 4-4 2026 Ravens, the question is whether their season is over. For the NFL franchise the Baltimore Ravens, the query is larger: Has their franchise player played his final down for the team? That’s a question for another day.

Today, the fallout is swift and debilitating. Jackson will miss at least four games on injured reserve and perhaps all nine of the Ravens’ remaining contests. They are in an even bigger lurch than losing a two-time MVP would typically put you in as they are also down their backup, Tyler Huntley. He’s battling a case of turf toe. It's expected to last weeks.

All of this as the Ravens have just 72 hours to prepare for Thursday evening’s game against the Jaguars. That means, absent a trade or free agent Hail Mary, it will be 25-year-old undrafted rookie “Joe Fagnano” under center vs. the Jags. It also means it will be a loss for the Ravens, and perhaps a complete loss for fantasy managers.

That’s because, for as well as Zay Flowers has played, there isn’t a whole lot that can be done when your quarterback is suddenly a guy who was playing for UConn this time last year. You will start Flowers, but you will no longer be counting on him to win your matchups. You just hope he doesn't lose them. It’s not quite as clear cut with Derrick Henry, but it’s ultimately difficult to envision the Big Dog on your bench. You just pray he cashes in one of the Ravens’ 1-2 red zone trips with a touchdown. For every other Raven, it’s see you whenever Jackson returns, which might be next year — or never.

Five Week 8 Storylines

Ashton Jeanty gets benched on early downs. Speaking during the week, Jeanty said the Jets couldn’t tackle. The Raiders coaching staff took care of that for them. Jeanty was sent to the pine, getting out-carried 25-2 by Mike Washington Jr. Message sent. We are less sure if it was received. That’s because Jeanty gained just 10 fewer yards on 20 fewer touches. He posted 73 tallies to MWJ’s 83. Washington got stuffed on one short-yardage carry after another, including at the goal line. Perhaps Klint Kubiak and company realized the Raiders’ rushing struggles aren’t all Jeanty’s fault after all. Fantasy managers have realized that Jeanty now has a touches dogfight on his hands, but with his dominance of the high-value handles through the air, Jeanty is probably still the preferred play on the digital gridiron.   

Jonah Coleman looks like the real deal in Broncos’ backfield. Although Coleman out-carried J.K. Dobbins just 11-7, he was the recipient of the Broncos’ goal-line work. He was also the only Denver running back to earn a target or catch a pass. The feared three-man committee with Tyler Badie or Cody Schrader never materialized. Fourth-round rookie Coleman is now 3-for-3 when it comes to earning a demonstrated commitment from famously fickle running backs coach Sean Payton. It’s time for fantasy managers to take notice, and get over their worries of Badie’s re-emergence. Even with only two teams on bye for Week 9, Coleman has earned his place in the RB2 ranks.

Vikings miss their shot in their easiest matchup. The Lions have the worst, or at least the most injured, pass defense in the NFL. Kyler Murray threw for 210 yards against them. It just isn’t going to happen for this ever frustrating, now clearly declining quarterback. It wasn’t happening for anyone in a Minnesota uniform on Sunday, as Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr.’s backfield committee produced thoroughly mediocre results. That could become a weekly occurrence with defenses realizing they are not going to be threatened by Murray. Although the Bills are a perfectly fine Week 9 matchup, we have gathered enough data points to know that for fantasy purposes, this offense is low-end WR1 Justin Jefferson and not a whole lot else,

Cam Ward finally makes real, tangible progress. Seemingly playing faster and looser, Ward had the first 300-yard game of his career. He averaged more than 9.0 yards per attempt for only the second time as a pro. Both his seven carries and 41 yards rushing were new career highs. Ward played a complete game, something made even more impressive by the fact that he was missing electric No. 1 receiver Carnell Tate. This being the Titans, the effort still came in a loss, but that’s now back-to-back encouraging performances for a quarterback who opened up 2026 as one of the league’s most disappointing players. Perhaps Ward will soon find himself in the streamer mix, but it won’t be in Week 10 when the Titans come off bye against the Jaguars.

Colts hit rock bottom, await trade deadline. The Colts did not compete in Jacksonville, not that they even wanted to. They did manage a pity touchdown for Josh Downs, who has somewhat absurdly requested a trade ahead of next Tuesday’s deadline. Maybe he’ll get it. The Colts certainly don’t need to keep their No. 3 wideout around for the rebuild. Although Downs has rather convincingly failed his latest fantasy test, he could still resuscitate his WR3 case if he ends up in the right landing spot. Meanwhile, the “right landing spot” would be just about anywhere else for Jonathan Taylor, who was used sparingly against the Jags, handling a season-low 62.3 percent of the snaps. As he awaits his fate, fantasy managers cannot wait any longer to take fliers on Seth McGowan and even second-year pro DJ Giddens.

Don't forget, for the latest on everything NFL, check out Rotoworld’s Player News, or follow @Rotoworld_FB or @RotoPat on Twitter/Bluesky.

Five More 8 Storylines

Things come undone for Cardinals — who still stun Cowboys. The Cardinals lost their No. 1 running back, No. 2 receiver and No. 3 running back to injury. They benched their starting quarterback. They, as you saw in the headline, won. Just another day in Jerryworld. While the media focus will be on the Cowboys’ misery, the fantasy focus shifts to the Cardinals’ quarterback. Who will it be for Week 9 in Seattle? Probably not Carson Beck. He has been banged up of late, and there would be perhaps no worse spot for a rookie to make their NFL debut. It’s also unlikely to be Jacoby Brissett following his benching. That leaves one option — Minshew Mania himself, Mr. Gardner. Will it work for long? No. Will it even work in Week 9? Also no. Does it build the Cardinals’ needed bridge to Beck? Yes. It’s also just enough to keep Michael Wilson and company fantasy relevant against the mighty Seahawks.

Emmett Johnson finally gets more involved as pass catcher. I’ve said it on so many podcasts I’ve lost count — “maybe this is finally the week the Chiefs get Emmett Johnson more involved as a receiver.” Sunday in Denver was finally that week, with Johnson leading the Chiefs in both aerial yards and yards from scrimmage while also posting the team’s longest gain, a 73-yard touchdown. Johnson was also grinding out tough gains on the ground, and might have finally made this a two-back backfield. That is nothing against Kenneth Walker III. It is something against the Chiefs’ skill corps talent. They are as starved for play-making ability as any team in the league, and besides Walker, it appears no Chief has more of it than rookie Johnson. If you’ve been stashing him on the deepest recesses of your 12-team league bench, it might finally be time to dust him off in Week 9 against the Jets.

Adonai Mitchell re-emerges to make Jets’ receiver corps more confusing than ever. We know not to overreact to one-game sample sizes like Mitchell’s Week 7 doughnut in his return to the lineup. But in our defense, it felt like more than one game. That’s because Mitchell’s marathon absence and dud of a return coincided with rookie Omar Cooper Jr.’s two-game hot streak. You could forgive us for connecting the dots. Well Sunday the dots scattered and fled. Mitchell had the best game of his career as Cooper failed to even see a target, let alone a catch. The takeaway is pretty much as feared: With Garrett Wilson still leading in looks, Mitchell and Cooper will be difficult to project on a weekly basis. Although they have the talent for more, they are best treated as boom/bust WR4s in this good but not great offense.

Chargers look just as broken coming out of their bye week. You could dress it up with whatever stats you like, fancy or otherwise, but the main takeaway is that the Bolts simply stunk yet again. There is so little talent on offense, and seemingly no one with a plan to scheme around that overriding problem. That leaves Justin Herbert as a sitting duck, and a panicked-processor too often making the wrong read because he just doesn’t want to get hit again. Although most fantasy players long ago gave up any hope of a turnaround, this dud coming out of the Chargers’ open date confirms Herbert is now a bottom-five quarterback, and no one besides Ladd McConkey has a real argument to be in 12-team league lineups, including Omarion Hampton.  

Hunter Henry injures foot vs. Dolphins, further depleting Pats skill corps. It didn’t matter for Drake Maye, who continued to successfully play pitch-and-catch, point guard football, but it is becoming a real problem for fantasy managers. Unlike the case at wide receiver — where none of DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams or Efton Chism are compelling 12-team league fill-ins for AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs — Henry at least has a 1-for-1 replacement in rookie Eli Raridon. The rook has made plays whenever given the chance this season, and with tight end up looking mighty thin in the 8-14 range, Raridon is very much worth a flier heading into Week 9.  

Questions

1. See what happens to the NFC East on days J.J. McCarthy doesn’t play?

2. Did the Chiefs ever consider it might be more beneficial to focus on scoring a touchdown rather than getting the clock to 0:00?

3. How does Gardner Minshew go Roger Staubach mode every time he sets foot in Jerryworld?

item.title: Jack Campbell injury: Live updates after Lions LB hospitalized with neck injury
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a scary-looking neck injury and was carted off the field. Here's the latest on his condition.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.

Campbell laid motionless on the turf at Ford Field after making a tackle against a fellow former Iowa Hawkeye, T.J. Hockenson. Down for more than 10 minutes, the scene in Detroit served as a sobering reminder of just how violent and dangerous football can be.

Campbell was immobilized, loaded onto a backboard and taken to the hospital, leading to an emotional on-field reaction from teammates.

Here's what to know about Campbell, inside and outside the white lines.

What happened to Jack Campbell?

Campbell went down with a neck injury after making a tackle against Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson in the fourth quarter.

He remained down on the field as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and the cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field.

Lions teammates took a knee and looked concerned as staff attended to him. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinsonwas in tears while the game was paused.

Latest Jack Campbell injury update

Campbell was resting and was scheduled to remain in a local hospital overnight for continued evaluation and monitoring, the Lions announced late Sunday night.

He was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury after exiting the team's Week 8 win over the Vikings.

Head coach Dan Campbell didn't have an update on the linebacker after the game.

"Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family," the coach said. "He's being taken care of. We don't have any new information."

When will there be an update on Jack Campbell's condition?

The Lions have not provided an update since late Sunday night and have not indicated when one might be available. However, coach Dan Campbell is scheduled to speak at 3 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 2, and will likely address Jack Campbell's injury.

Who is Jack Campbell?

Campbell is a linebacker for the Detroit Lions.

The 26-year-old is in his fourth NFL season, all with Detroit. Campbell was drafted by the Lions with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft after starring in college for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 in addition to receiving the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football.

He also received the William V. Campbell Trophy, also known as the "academic Heisman," in 2022 for being recognized as the college football player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance.

Campbell slid right in as a key piece to the Lions defense following his arrival in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season.

On May 21, 2026, the Lions recognized Campbell's breakout with a four-year, $81 million extension.

Prior to his injury in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, Campbell hadn't missed a game in his four-year career.

Is Jack Campbell married?

Campbell has been married to his wife, Megan, since June 2024.

View this post on Instagram

The couple met during their time together at Iowa, where Megan also starred as an athlete on the women's basketball team.

"We were both college athletes required to spend the summer training for our respective sports," the couple wrote on their wedding website. "We owe it all to Peterson Dorm in Iowa City where we became great friends before eventually dating the following fall of our sophomore year."

Formerly known as Megan Meyer, she finished her college basketball career at Drake.

Does Jack Campbell have kids?

The Campbell family welcomed their first child, Cooper James, on July 3, 2026. Megan shared the news on Instagram with the caption:

"Cooper James Campbell 🤍7/3 - The beginning of our favorite chapter yet! We love you so much buddy 💌."

View this post on Instagram

The couple announced on Instagram in February that they were expecting.

View this post on Instagram

Were Jack Campbell and T.J. Hockenson teammates at Iowa?

Campbell and Hockenson were not teammates.

The linebacker started his Hawkeye career in 2019, the same year that Hockenson was drafted by the Lions. The tight end was selected with the No. 8 pick in the 2019 NFL Draft by the Lions, but the two never crossed paths in college despite both starring at Iowa.

Were Jack Campbell and T.J. Hockenson teammates on the Lions?

Campbell and Hockenson weren't teammates with the Lions.

Like ships in the night, Hockenson was exiting as Campbell entered. The tight end was traded from the Lions to the Minnesota Vikings during the 2022 season, marking the end of his time in the Motor City.

Campbell was drafted by Detroit during the following offseason.

Aidan Hutchinson reacts to Jack Campbell injury

As the Campbell situation unfolded on the field, NFL on Fox camera showed an emotional Hutchinson, clearly shaken by what happened to his teammate.

An emotional @aidanhutch97 being a leader for the @Lions defense after Jack Campbell was carted off. pic.twitter.com/ssy0VQVlNi

— FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026

Hutchinson was attempting to rally his defense as medical staff tended to Campbell. He spoke about it after the game.

"It's a scary thing," Hutchinson said. "I wouldn't wish it on anybody."

He spoke about the helpless feeling of being on the cart and then highlighted how much Campbell means to the team.

"He's everything, man," Hutchinson said. "He's a captain, leader, teammate, husband, father, everything. We're all praying for him."

Jared Goff reacts to Jack Campbell injury

Quarterback Jared Goff told reporters after the game that Campbell's injury was a reality check.

"Definitely scary and just brings you back to reality for a moment," Goff said. "He's a husband and a father. We're praying for him and hoping he's gonna be alright. If I know anyone that's tough enough to get through something like that, it's gonna be him."

The quarterback pointed out that it isn't easy to get back into the game after a major injury like that.

"It's always so surreal, stuff like that happens, blow the whistle and we're off again," Goff said after the game. "It's hard. It's really hard and I think you gotta remind these guys are humans and deal with stuff."

DJ Reed reacts to Jack Campbell injury

Reed chose to focus on Campbell the person instead of Campbell the player after the game. The cornerback told reporters that there is a lot that goes through your mind during those moments, saying that they are praying for him and his family.

item.title: Saints still deciding if Jordyn Tyson, Travis Etienne will return to practice this week
item.description: The Saints have yet to see rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson in game action, but they would move closer to that moment if the first-round pick is designated for return from injured reserve this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints have yet to see rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson in game action, but they would move closer to that moment if the first-round pick is designated for return from injured reserve this week.

Tyson has been out since injuring his hamstring this summer and head coach Kellen Moore told reporters on Monday that the team is still working through a decision on opening the wideout's return window. If he does practice Wednesday, Tyson will have 21 days to work with the team before he must be activated and he can be activated at any point in that window.

Moore said the case is similar for running back Travis Etienne and left tackle Kelvin Banks. Etienne has been out since Week 3 with a hamstring injury and Banks sprained his ankle in Week 2.

Getting all three back would be a positive development for the Saints offense as the team tries to improve on a 2-5 start to the season.

item.title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Bolts earn ‘D’ in loss to Rams
item.description: The Chargers received a very poor grade from CBS Sports for their equally-poor performance on offense vs. the Rams.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers led the Rams with less than two minutes remaining in the first half. By the time they went into the locker room, they were down 10-9. The final score was 24-9.

It was another disaster ending to a game in which the Chargers showed “something.”

They had three drives reach the red zone and they only managed three field goals. That wasn’t enough in a game where the Rams offense was held without a first down until that very last drive of the first half.

It’s a sad time when the offense almost looks “good” after scoring nine points, but that’s how low the bar was set after their first six games.

CBS Sports’ John Breech felt exactly the way Chargers fans probably did watching Sunday’s loss. That’s why he gave the Bolts a “D” grade for their seventh consecutive loss to begin the season.

“The Chargers offense is broken. This team had a bye in Week 7 to get things fixed, and somehow they actually looked worse. One problem is that Justin Herbert looks like a shell of his former self. Herbert has turned the ball over at least once in every game this season and he added to that total with two bad interceptions against the Rams. It’s very possible that he’s just not a fit for Mike McDaniel’s and if that’s the case, then the Chargers might want to think about moving on from McDaniel.”
