item.title: AFC Playoff Picture after Week 8: Chiefs fall into Wild Card mix
item.description: Here’s where things stand in the race for the AFC postseason and where Kansas City fits in.
item.content:encoded:
With just an NFC matchup to go in the NFL’s Week 8 schedule, it’s a good time to look at the updated AFC playoff picture after the Kansas City Chiefs’ season-altering loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday afternoon.

AFC Standings

Going into Week 9

1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) — AFC East leader
2. Denver Broncos (6-2) — AFC West leader
3. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) — AFC North leader
4. Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) — AFC South leader

    As of now, the Bills are in the driver’s seat to earning a postseason bye and making the conference’s road to Super Bowl LXI go through New Highmark Stadium. The Chiefs’ matchup with Buffalo on Thanksgiving night could be Kansas City’s final chance to stay alive for the No.1 seed.

    Jacksonville currently sits as the lowest seed among the division leaders because of an early bye week, but the Jaguars lead the NFL in point differential (+85) and look like the most complete team in the conference right now.

    Denver’s 3-1 record in the AFC so far gives them a current leg up over Pittsburgh (3-2).

    5. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2)
    6. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2)
    7. New England Patriots (5-3)

    The Patriots currently hold the tiebreaker over another 5-3 AFC playoff contender — the Cleveland Browns — due to a 5-1 record against conference opponents compared to Cleveland’s 3-3 mark.

    The Chiefs are also 5-1 against AFC teams so far, giving them a leg up on the Bengals, who are 4-2 in-conference.

    Cincinnati lost its first head-to-head matchup with division-leading Pittsburgh, but the rematch is in a couple of weeks and could vault the Bengals into the top-4 seeds.

    8. Cleveland Browns (5-3)
    9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-4)
    10. Baltimore Ravens (4-4)

    The remaining AFC teams with records at or above .500 could make things interesting any given Sunday, but don’t feel as threatening as the seven teams currently in the playoff picture.

    The Chiefs will still play the Bills, the Bengals, and the Patriots this season.

item.title: Grade the NFL Trade: Bears trade for Jeffery Simmons gets an A
item.description: High marks for the Chicago Bears trade for Jeffery Simmons!
item.content:encoded:
After the Chicago Bears traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, we asked you to grade the trade, and most of you gave it high marks.

We obviously won’t know the true cost of the deal for a few years, but this is a win-now move for a team that feels it’s in a Super Bowl window. The Bears have the head coach and the quarterback they feel can win with, so sending a 2027 and 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick was what it took to bring in a red-level talent for a defense lacking star power.

In his eight-year career, Simmons has been named to four Pro Bowls and three All-Pro Teams. He’s coming off a First Team All-Pro nod after racking up a career-high 11 sacks in 15 games for the Titans. The move from the one-win Titans to the 5-2 Bears will boost his profile and improve his chances of winning the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have those odds at +2000, which are the seventh-best.

The Bears play on prime time the next two weeks and have two more standalone games slated for Thanksgiving and Christmas, so if Simmons helps turn Chicago’s defense around, he’ll definitely be in the mix.

item.title: Cam Ward needs to build on yesterday’s performance against Bengals
item.description: Is the former first overall pick finally ready to take a leap?
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday was Cam Ward’s best performance with the Tennessee Titans. He threw for 304 yards and rushed for 41. It was by far the most comfortable he has looked with Brian Daboll as his offensive coordinator. It is hopefully a performance that he can build on going forward.

The best outcome for the Titans is for Ward to develop into the quarterback they thought he could be when they selected him with the first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Even with most people, myself included, thinking Ward doesn’t have it in him, there is still time for him to prove that wrong. Consistency is going to be the key for him. We saw a couple of really good performances from him last season, but he was never able to stack positive games.

It’s a shame the Titans have their bye this week right when it looks like the offense is finally starting to come together. The Titans play the Jacksonville Jaguars, Dallas Cowboys, the Jaguars again, and the Washington Commanders coming out of the bye. All three of those teams are pretty bad against the pass. In fact, the Indianapolis Colts, who rank 12th in passing yards per game allowed, are the best defense that the Titans face the rest of the way. Let’s see if they can take advantage.

And one note for those of you worried about draft position: the Titans’ defense ranks 31st against the pass this season. If the Titans are going to win any of those games, they are going to have to consistently get into the high 20s or 30s to have a chance to win. They did it yesterday, but that was just one game. Based on the balance of what we have seen this year, I wouldn’t bet on that happening, but hey, at least shootout losses are fun to watch.

item.title: Fantasy Football: Bhayshul Tuten bringing the explosives, plus more key stats from Week 8 that may go overlooked
item.description: Joel Smyth highlights key stats from Week 8 you should know to help with fantasy football moving forward.
item.content:encoded:
In fantasy football, you have to look back to move forward. Fantasy points are the goal, but how a player gets there is the key. Analyst Joel Smyth breaks down eight numbers to know from Week 8 in order to win your matchup in Week 9 and beyond.

25-2

The Las Vegas RB carry split between Mike Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty, favoring Washington. Jeanty's 69% rush share vanished in a flash. The long-awaited fear came true on Sunday as Klint Kubiak went with Washington as the RB1, with Jeanty still managing injury and struggling behind the Raiders offensive line. Jeanty only played 25 snaps, 15 being pass routes, bringing in three of his four targets. Kubiak denied the idea that Jeanty was limited due to his comments to the media earlier this week, making his future very scary for fantasy managers. When Jeanty was getting elite fantasy volume, it was only equaling low-level RB1 numbers. Now without it, Jeanty could be unplayable, with a passing-down role being the only thing to hang onto.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Mike Washington Jr.’s featured role at running back was “my call” and noted Ashton Jeanty is “still going to be a big part of our team.”

Asked Kubiak if Jeanty’s limited workload had anything to do with his mid-week comments in the media.… pic.twitter.com/rkzCdWdsbg

— Sam Gordon (@BySamGordon) November 1, 2026

Washington had all six goal-line carries, ultimately facing the same fate as Jeanty with zero scores, for what it's worth. 

3

Targets for Quinshon Judkins since Dylan Sampson returned in Week 7. Prior to last week, Quinshon Judkins had 50% of his fantasy points in PPR leagues come from receiving, one of the highest in the NFL, although we think of him as a bruiser. Well, with Sampson back in the lineup, he's back to being a bruiser only. It can work as it did last week in a big way, rushing for two touchdowns and 96 yards versus a porous Titans defense, but when it matchups against teams such as Pittsburgh, it becomes much more difficult. Cleveland simply winning games has been huge for Judkins. However, when the Browns are forced into pass-heavy weeks, he's just not on the field enough. Sampson's 47 routes to Judkins' 19 in the last two games have resulted in the Browns starter being limited to 6.2 receiving points. He's no longer game-script proof. 

6

Fantasy opportunities for Jonah Coleman at the goal line in Week 8, including one target resulting in a penalty. Elite usage for the rookie in the most important area of the field, ultimately getting into the end zone on his sixth chance. The Broncos will throw to their running backs plenty in the red zone and even at the goal line. With Coleman having both the RJ Harvey receiving role combined with his usage on the ground, the touchdown potential is tremendous. Coleman had all five running back targets and, in the second half, had 8-of-8 RB touches. Denver is a top-10 team in RB fantasy points, and it's looking like Coleman will have the valuable work with an amazing ROS schedule ahead: CAR, LV, PIT, MIA, NYJ, LV, BUF, NE.

4

Explosive plays by Bhayshul Tuten in his last two games, after four in his first five games to begin the season. Tuten was having a solid fantasy start to his sophomore campaign with a slowly growing role and a couple of touchdowns. The volume kept growing, the Jaguars offense kept cooking but something was missing. The RB who was constantly bursting through holes at blazing speeds wasn't breaking off the huge explosive plays, and if he did, they were called back by penalties (so many times). That's all changed the last couple of weeks. Entering Week 6, Tuten had four explosive plays for 8.3 fantasy points. Since then, his four explosive plays have gone for over 33 fantasy points. The ability was there, the luck wasn't and, for Tuten believers, it's all come together. Tuten should be seen as a borderline RB1 the rest of the season. 

29.6%

The rate of targets per route for Rashee Rice in his return, 0.1% higher than his 2025 season mark. Rice built off his last full game with another high-volume performance, bringing in seven of his eight targets for 53 yards and a TD. Rice had plenty of work underneath and was the main target in the receiving game, with three designed targets, including one more called back by penalty. Off the hamstring injury, Rice was limited in his routes as a whole, only on the field for 64% of pass plays. As the season continues, Rice’s playing time and efficiency can increase over time, not just from the hamstring, but from his preseason injuries as well. 

Rashee Rice is back

slant. screen. and now a 10 yard TD off mesh

— Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) November 1, 2026

0.50

Fantasy points per route run by DJ Moore, 13th among WRs. The injuries have been frustrating and have likely killed your fantasy team multiple times already, but when he has been on the field, Moore's been what you drafted him to be. The volume is that of a WR1. He's led the Bills in targets in all three games he's completed, getting downfield shots that have been proven valuable with Josh Allen at QB. The passing volume in Buffalo won't be consistent, but Moore being tied to a top-five offense as the clear No. 1 option makes him a great asset. Because of the injuries and limited time, Moore still may not be seen as a top fantasy WR, but I believe he deserves to be with the volume he's seen in the Buffalo offense. 

15

Fantasy PPG for Jaylen Waddle when Bo Nix throws for 200+ passing yards. That has been half of the Broncos' eight games, with Nix averaging 136 yards in the other weeks. It's been a rough start for the Broncos' passing attack, and I've stood on the same point with Waddle, being: he'll go as the offense goes. It hasn't just been him. Denver's WRs are 27th in fantasy points in 2026 after ranking ninth in 2025. Nix only has one game over 225 passing yards, Week 2 versus Jacksonville (Waddle's best week), compared to eight games of over 240 yards last season. The new Broncos WR has still led the team in targets in six of the last seven games and can be a second-half riser if Nix can also be a second-half riser. Everything positive from the preseason is still there, and if Nix can build on the last couple of weeks, Waddle can fight his way off the bust list.

Week 4: 14.5 pts

Targets per route run for Adonai Mitchell this season, the highest on the Jets, and 15th among all NFL wide receivers. I don't need to continue talking about Geno Smith's love for his young wideout, but it is an important note for Mitchell's potential and Garrett Wilson's as well. Mitchell won't suddenly be a stable fantasy WR2, but will have the ceiling potential we've seen already from him and Omar Cooper Jr. He will also have the same floor as Cooper on Sunday: 0 points on 0 targets. Wilson still got his, but it's yet another obstacle for the early-round fantasy WR to overcome. The Jets have said they need to get Wilson more targets, but I find it hard to believe it gets much better with Mitchell, Cooper, and others consistently making their mark.

item.title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week eight defeat
item.description: Chop Robinson was quarterback hunting on Sunday, while Jonah Savaiinaea struggled to protect his own signal-caller.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins took a ten-point lead into halftime on Sunday against the hated New England Patriots. Unfortunately, they were dominated in the second half of play — being outscored by Drake Maye and company 21-6 while ultimately falling by a final score of 24-19 on a soggy day in South Florida.

While losing is never fun, the Dolphins continue to play their opponents tough each and every week. I forecast better days ahead for this organization when general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan is able to infuse the roster with more talent this offseason.

FINS UP

Our Fins Up player of the week is pass rusher Chop Robinson. Robinson finished Sunday’s game against New England with three tackles and two sacks of opposing quarterback Drake Maye according to Pro Football Reference.

In addition to his two sacks, Robinson had eight pressures on the day — good for a 47.1% pressure rate against New England according to Hussam Patel of the 5 Reasons Sports Network. That mark is the second-highest pressure rate of any NFL defender in a single game this season. Miami’s pass rusher now leads the National Football League in pressure rate with a 26.6% mark for the entire year.

FINS DOWN

Our Fins Down player is Jonah Savaiinaea. Miami’s second-year offensive lineman had been trending up through the first portion of the season when you compared his play to that of his abysmal rookie season. Sundays game against the Patriots was more reminiscent of his dreadful rookie season than his promising second year. Miami’s starting left guard, Kadyn Proctor, missed Sunday’s game due to a concussion, which caused center Aaron Brewer to have to help his replacement, Jarrett Kingston, more than he was able to help Savaiinaea against New England. That was not a recipe for success.

While Miami’s starting right guard has delivered massive improvement in 2026, Sunday’s poor showing proves he still has plenty of work to do if he wants to consider himself a quality starting offensive lineman in the National Football League. Savaiinaea and the entire Dolphins offense should benefit from the return of Proctor this upcoming Sunday when Miami hosts the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens.

item.title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Dolphins
item.description: Notes, thoughts and observations from Sunday’s Patriots win.
item.content:encoded:
Allow me to be the first to welcome everyone to the best time of the year! 3:30 p.m. sunsets and constant darkness, here we come!

It’s wild how I used to actually enjoy the first night of Daylight Savings Time starting, or ending, or whichever one this one is. You’re out at the bars, they’re about to close…and then all of a sudden, you get an extra hour to make bad decisions. But I’ve aged out of all that, alas, so now I’m taking up the mantle of the crotchety middle-aged man who likes to complain about everything.

At least I’m not complaining about a Patriots loss, though, as New England took care of business to the tune of a 24-19 victory to move ahead to 5-3, 3-0 in the AFC East.

  1. I had absolutely no idea what to expect coming into this game. Sure, the Fins stink, but nothing is as it seems when the Patriots head down to Miami. Compound that with rainy conditions, an oddly-positioned 4:25 slot for a game that certainly didn’t deserve a late window, and an absolutely decimated Patriots team, and this just seemed to have all the makings of a trap game.
  2. And for the first half, that’s exactly what seemed to be happening. New England couldn’t move the ball at all, the defense was oddly off, and the whole game just seemed like holiday commercials before Halloween even hits; nobody wants to see that. But something happened in that locker room at halftime, because the Patriots came out and scored on three consecutive drives to open this one up.
  3. But I’m getting ahead of myself. I have a few more complaints to lodge before I break this game down in earnest.
  4. As the Patriots played in the late window for the first time this year, I watched the 1 p.m. games for the first time all season. And I wish I was saying differently, but the NFL is becoming completely unwatchable. The games have zero flow to them. The officiating somehow seems to be getting worse every year as opposed to better, and everyone just kind of stinks. As a product, it has been trending in the wrong direction for years now, and I’m starting to wonder when I’m going to just stop watching altogether.
  5. Probably when the NFL inevitably starts offering Tuesday Night Football, Wednesday Night Football, and Friday Night Football to completely oversaturate the market. Children would love to eat chocolate and candy with every meal, but normal adults don’t allow that. You need to limit things.
  6. OK, enough of that. Sorry to open on a downer. I just used to love the NFL so damn much, and it’s losing me, and that makes me sad.
  7. On the plus side, the horrendous officiating and terrible refs blessed us with what might be the most spectacular display of infathomable incompetence we’re going to see this year. On New England’s second possession of the third quarter, Drake Maye hit Kyle Williams for what turned out to be a 43-yard touchdown. Williams caught the ball at the five-yard line, took four or five steps, crossed the goal line, then his knee hit the ball and came loose. The goal-line referee threw a blue beanbag to indicate a loose ball/fumble, and then ruled the pass incomplete. The result was Mike Vrabel suddenly finding himself on the radar of no fewer than six QB-needy teams as he threw an absolute laser of a challenge flag 65 yards in order to get the call…I don’t even want to say “reversed,” as there were about six different things that went wrong for the refs there. Just pure, unadulterated comedy.
  8. What isn’t funny, though, is playing a game without your WR1, WR2, TE1, LG1, LG2, RB2, RG1, and RG2. I don’t know who any of these people are.
  9. I’m just going to hope that the Patriots were being extra cautious with these guys and were confident that they could beat Miami wildly short-handed, because the Packers and Lions are coming up and this simply isn’t sustainable.
  10. Thank Tebow that we have Drake Maye, as that man put the franchise on his back yesterday and didn’t look back. He’s finding ways to make plays and extend drives with the guys he has. I’d be lying if I said that I didn’t think that New England was done for once Hunter Henry went back to the locker room, but New England dug deep into the well, operated out of a lot ot Jumbo sets featuring tight end extraordinaire Caleb Lomu on the end, ground it out with Stevenson, and utilized the run to open up the big play. The Williams and Pop Douglas catches ended up being what decided this one.
  11. Was it the Williams touchdown where a Dolphins defender had Maye dead to rights on an unimpeded blitz, but instead just kind of fell down and didn’t even touch him? Or maybe it was the fourth-down conversion to Efton Chism that could have completely changed the momentum of the entire game if he had just done anything besides fall down. Dolphins gonna Dolphin, I guess.
  12. Though I don’t know how the refs were able to overturn that DeMario Douglas fourth-down conversion that was/wasn’t/was. I’m always blown away by how different my interpretation of the phrase “incontrovertible evidence” is from the NFL’s.
  13. My favorite play of the game had to be Maye’s TD run, a read-option where he completely froze Willie Gay and Rajon Rondo’d his way into the end zone. Just a beautiful read, pump fake, and play design. Morgan Moses knew Maye could handle Gay, so he bumped up to chip block Uche and leave a wide open lane. These jumbo packages are going to be a lot of fun when the Patriots actually have some receivers in there.
  14. Was anybody else screaming a combination of “Don’t fall down!” and “Hang onto the ball, dammit!” as Douglas was weaving his way towards the end zone?
  15. You know who I don’t want or need to talk about this morning? Will Campbell. Who played half of the game next to Walter Rouse, who was pulled for a Ben Brown who basically had to get in and out of a hospital bed in between drives. 27 passing snaps, just one hurry allowed. There’s a very large faction of fans out there who lament the fact that the Patriots got Campbell instead of trading down and taking Tetairoa McMillan… but if Campbell wasn’t out there, this 2026 unit would probably have Milton Williams trying to set the edge on offense.
  16. Who I do need to talk about, though, is Jared Wilson. I’m going to be nice and chalk yesterday up to a combination of the wet weather and the rain shrinking that protective layer on Wilson’s helmet, which restricted blood flow to his brain, because he seemed to think he was playing Bocce instead of snapping a football on multiple occasions.
  17. This is one of those offensive performances where you’re able to be happy with what you saw, acknowledge that it could have been better, and also acknowledge that this isn’t sustainable with the current roster. Mack Hollins should be eligible to return this week, and hopefully the Patriots just held AJ Brown out this week as a precaution.
  18. Oh, and hopefully Hunter Henry is OK. And Gabe Jacas.
  19. Speaking of Jacas, who continues to be a disruptive force… this was a weird game for the defense. They were well-disciplined and decisive up front, but still allowed Malik Willis to move the ball. No Miami receiver eclipsed 50 yards… but the D gave up key plays in big moments. I haven’t watched any replay footage, but this team seems to feast in man and famine in zone. If I had to guess, I’d say that Zak Kuhr called a lot of zone looks yesterday. The Dolphins responded with underneath routes and sit-down routes to efficiently move the chains. New England gave up completions of 35, 23, 19, and 18 yards. I have always been of the opinion that the only place you want to see a soft cushion is on a chair, but I know multiple DCs that disagree with me.
  20. I’d like to show Logan Ryan some love, as I think he was a very underrated Patriots DB and had some great moments in New England. And as a commentator, he’s still pretty green with plenty of time and room to find his footing. But I don’t think you’ll be seeing him call any of the bigger games anytime soon.
  21. I have about as much faith in Andy Borregales as I do in men whose Halloween costume is an oversized gift label with TO: WOMEN FROM: GOD written on it. And Mike Vrabel seems to feel the same way, as the Patriots seem to view anything on the opponent’s side of the field and less than five yards to go as instant four-down territory.
  22. The Patriots are currently sitting at 5-3 as we approach what used to be the nice, clean, halfway point of the season. They’re a game and a half behind the Bills for the division with the entire AFC kind of a jumble right now. I could see them going 3-6 over the last nine games just as easily as I could see them going 7-2. I guess it depends on how many more players get hurt and how quickly guys can return.

I hope everyone had a fun, safe, and happy Halloween. This was the last time we’ll see Halloween fall on a Saturday night until 2037, so hopefully you got some good shenanigans in. Now if you’ll excuse me, I’m going to run to the pharmacy before they change the shelves and all of the Christmas stuff goes up.

item.title: Will the Broncos’ big win against the Chiefs make them NFL trade deadline buyers?
item.description: Another gutsy performance by the Denver Broncos has catapulted them to the top of the AFC West. Will that cause them to go all-in as buyers at the NFL trade deadline?
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos are the comeback kings of the National Football League. Yesterday, they once again embarked on fourth quarter heroics to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-2. At 6-2, the Broncos are now in first place of the AFC West.

It was another gutsy and gritty performance by Denver. Emblematic of the type of team they’ve forged into since Head Coach Sean Payton took over in 2023. It’s the fifteenth game in a row the Broncos have won in one-score affairs. It was the 200th victory of Payton’s remarkable career.

Encapsulating how the team keeps finding a way to grind out big wins in key moments isn’t easy. However, Payton did his best to answer when he felt the Broncos had found their groove as a legitimate contender and went back to last October which was the beginning of a long winning streak for the franchise.

“I think honestly, to answer that, I think it has to come from, well, we did it before. I would go back to Philly [2025] at Philly after playing Cincinnati on a Monday. I think that’s the first—that would be where my brain would go where we grew a little bit,” stated Payton.

“Then there’s a belief that can get stronger and then there’s experience. Then you’re seasoned a little, but we still have a lot of things to fix. I honestly think that’s where I believe it comes from.”

The Broncos didn’t play their best game against the Chiefs in Week 8. Nevertheless, they came out as the victors. Tough teams find a way to win when the stakes are high. Reeling off fifteen fourth quarter points, Bo Nix and Denver’s offense found good footing in critical moments and came away with two big scoring drives.

A big part of their success was featuring rookie running back Jonah Coleman. He was missing in action for most of the first half, but Payton dedicated virtually all of the team’s backfield snaps to Coleman in the final two quarters of play. The fourth-round pick wound up with 104 all-purpose yards and 1 touchdown and flashed as a runner and receiver out of the backfield.

After the game, Coleman reflected on his performance humbly. He emphasized the importance of teamwork and also praised Broncos Country for showing up. Coleman, like many other players and coaches, all pointed to the noise from fans as being instrumental on the victory—especially at the end with the defense’s impeccable goal line stand.

“Like I said, glory be to God, he allowed me to do what I love. I just got to give a shoutout to my offensive line and my teammates for keeping the confidence up the whole game. The game didn’t go our way the whole entire game until the fourth quarter,” stated Coleman.

“I went up to all the offensive lineman, the receivers, and the defense and said, ‘It’s going to be a four-quarter game,’ like coach said—just to remind them it’s not over. So, when the fourth quarter hit, that’s when the spark just lit up in the whole team.”

The Broncos have now won four games in a row. They are heating up as each week passes. This coming Sunday, they travel to the east coast to take on the Carolina Panthers. If Denver can continue to improve and take care of business on the road, they will enter their bye week at 7-2. All things considered that would be quite remarkable.

The big question between now and then is whether or not yesterday’s huge win will cause Denver’s front office to be major buyers before the November 10th trade deadline. Had they lost and went to 5-3, I’m not certain that would have been the case.

But now? They have a really good shot at winning the division if they perform well down the stretch. Moreover, a chance at earning the number one seed again in a tough AFC playoff race. Have they seen enough from the players they have in the fold to make a Super Bowl push? Or do they believe there is a piece or two missing that need to be added to achieve this year’s gridiron goal?

The clock is ticking and I can’t wait to see what happens in that regard.

item.title: Eagles News: Nick Sirianni’s seat is getting hotter
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/2/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

The Eagles certainly have issues that go beyond their head coach. But if you’re not part of the solution, you’re part of the problem. And Nick Sirianni doesn’t seem to have answers. This is a poorly coached team. I struggle to see Sirianni returning in 2027 if the team helplessly continues their downward spiral.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Nick Sirianni’s Eagles are burning. Jeffrey Lurie may prefer his Eagles rise from the ashes of Sirianni’s tenure. – Inquirer

Sirianni, meanwhile, has nine games left to salvage this season and save it from becoming a referendum on his ability to lead the Eagles out of their doldrums. Lurie may not want to live through a repeat of 2012, 2015 or 2020. But each lost season resulted in him firing his coach, and if he’s being honest with himself, a rebirth. That isn’t an endorsement to get rid of Sirianni. But Lurie entertained the idea before (see: after the 2023 season and during the 2024 bye), and it’s just difficult to see another offseason of the Eagles explaining another change at offensive coordinator. They may end up doing that, but with a new head coach who is also their preferred coordinator. Doug Pederson lost his job partly because he refused to alter his coaching suggestions following the 2020 season. Sirianni has allowed Lurie and Roseman to influence some of his hires. It’s hard to believe they didn’t have some say in him bringing Sean Mannion and his scheme to Philadelphia. But Sirianni said he is still sticking by Mannion and his assistants.

10 Eagles things I think I think from the loss to the Commanders – BGN

9) This team quit for the second straight week. Nick Sirianni protected his players last week by saying he didn’t see an effort issue against the Cowboys. Even if Sirianni fudged the truth to the media, that was the right thing to do as he likely spoke to his players about the lack of effort when evaluating the film. The Eagles demonstrated a lack of effort again with 1:52 left in the game, when the Commanders went for two in a 25-10 game that was all but decided. The decision was wise by the Commanders, as a conversion gets them up three scores with barely any time left — an outcome that would make it basically impossible for the Eagles to tie the game (yet alone win). The defensive line didn’t even try to stop Austin Ekeler from going into the end zone. They checked out, much like the team did on several plays throughout last week’s game. This is a culture problem for the Eagles, and a bad look for a head coach that prides himself on culture. The film doesn’t lie regarding the Eagles’ effort over the last two weeks.

Eagles-Commanders Postgame: Tanner McKee, Eagles DUMPED ON, Lose Sixth Straight – PHLY Eagles

Despite squirreling out to an early 10-0 lead, the Philadelphia Eagles lost their sixth straight game to the lowly Washington Commanders in a game filled with familiar F-ups, like pre-snap penalties, bewildering play-calling, bizarre injury mismanagement, sloppy defense and more. Let’s talk about it with Brandon Lee Gowton, Bo Wulf, Miles Johnson, Fran Duffy, Vinny Curry and EJ Smith.

Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Commanders game – PhillyVoice

Anytime the team — maybe more specifically the offense — has gone through some rough patches, Sirianni has maintained positivity. Some go-to phrases might include “We’re close,” or “We have to lean on the things we do well.” But not after this game. Not after this six-game losing streak. Sirianni couldn’t muster any positivity. His candor was refreshing in a way, but also perhaps confirmation of what many have seen from this team all season… that nobody has any answers, and it doesn’t feel at all like any are forthcoming.

Another L – Iggles Blitz

Nick Sirianni looked like a beaten down man in his press conference. He is unbelievably frustrated by all the mistakes this team makes. He can live with talent issues. That is what you have to deal with when backups get on the field. But guys not getting line up correctly is unacceptable. Defenders not setting the edge is unacceptable. Missed blocking assignments are unacceptable. Sirianni likes his teams to be great at the things that don’t require talent. This group isn’t close to great when it comes to that stuff. They make dumb mistakes, often at the worst times. Something is just off. There are a ton of questions, but very few answers right now. Sirianni and his staff need to keep searching for solutions. There is still a lot of football left to play. It would certainly help to get some injured players back. Still, as I mentioned earlier, the problems go well beyond injuries

If Eagles fire Nick Sirianni, here are 5 candidates to replace him, including ex-Philly coach – NJ.com

Grant Udinski will be one of the top head-coaching candidates during the 2027 interview cycle. At 31, he would be the youngest head coach in the NFL. The Eagles would be taking a big risk hiring the league’s youngest head coach, but the reward could be great. The Rams hired Sean McVay at age 30 — and look at how that turned out. McVay has become one of the NFL’s best head coaches and one of the best offensive coaches in league history. He’s been to two Super Bowls, with one title. Udinski could solve the Eagles’ offensive problems in a way no other coach has. He has learned from Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and Jaguars head coach Liam Cohen, two of the league’s elite offensive play callers. He could help the Eagles install a better version of the Kyle Shanahan-McVay system.

Nick Sirianni: I am not doing a good enough job, I’ve got to do better – PFT

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took the blame after Sunday night’s loss to the Commanders. The Eagles, who started the season 2-0 and had Super Bowl aspirations, lost their sixth consecutive game to fall to 2-6. Sirianni said the head coach deserves the blame when that happens. “I take everything as my responsibility that happens out on that field. Everything. Obviously I am not doing a good enough job right now. I’ve got to do better,” Sirianni said. Asked if offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will remain the play caller, Sirianni didn’t answer directly.

Eagles-Commanders instant takeaways: Mental miscues extend losing streak to six … is this rock bottom? – PHLY Sports

Mixed McKee. This was an uneven game for Tanner McKee. The backup quarterback had stretches where he seemed more settled operating Sean Mannion’s system and there were even some glimpses of an identity forming with him under center on the Eagles’ opening series. He found Saquon Barkley for a chunk gain thanks to a well-designed pass play to Barkley on a wheel route out of a “spinner-series” play-action fake out of the backfield. He also managed a well-layered throw to Makai Lemon on a deep crossing route. That was the good. The bad came mostly from McKee navigating muddy pockets. He can be absolved for a handful of errant throws with things collapsing around him and a steadier-than-ideal number of unblocked rushers making things complicated. But with the Eagles on the edge of field-goal range late in the third quarter, McKee not only took a sack in a clear “can’t take a sack here” scenario, he lost the ball as well. Overall, McKee finished 18-for-28 with 139 yards, one interception and one lost fumble. One week after seemingly making some progress, this was about as ugly as it’s been for McKee in another peformance mostly defined by mistakes.

Roob’s Observations as Eagles’ disastrous streak continues in loss to Commanders – NBCSP

Now we can all stop pretending that they have any chance of winning the NFC East, even when the NFC East is the worst division in football. We can stop pretending they are going to wake up and suddenly start playing like the playoff team we expected before the season began, like the team that won a Super Bowl just 21 months ago. We can stop playing those games. They’re not good. In fact, they’re really, really bad. The questions facing the franchise now are how dramatic must the changes be, not just after the season but next week at the trade deadline. And not just on the roster but on the coaching staff as well, from the position coaches to the coordinators and all the way up to the head coach. How much do you consider Jalen Hurts’ situation when figuring out how significant those changes have to be? And how many of the over-priced, under-achieving players on this defense are worth keeping around? So many questions. But at least now Jeff Lurie and Howie Roseman can focus on the future instead of hoping something will click this year. It won’t click. It’s over.

Albert Breer’s Week 8 NFL Takeaways: Why These Bengals Are Different Than Previous Teams – SI

The Eagles are all alone in last place in the division this late in the season for the first time in forever. And while I have a hard time seeing running back Saquon Barkley on this list, there are a number of guys on one-year deals (Dallas Goedert, Tariq Woolen, Hollywood Brown) who should be available.

NFL Week 8: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games – ESPN

Will the Eagles be sellers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline? At 2-6, hope for a turnaround is fading fast. Working with a backup quarterback in McKee and a reworked offensive line that is having trouble holding up, the offense doesn’t have anything to rely on, especially with running back Saquon Barkley limited and the Eagles’ top receivers ailing. And the defense isn’t generating a consistent pass rush. General manager Howie Roseman will not be in fire-sale mode, but as he showed already with the Cam Jurgens trade, he won’t be afraid to act if it’s the right deal. Philadelphia will hold on to its cornerstone players, but those who are not in the long-term plans could be targeted by teams around the league as the Eagles continue to collect picks in the 2027 and ’28 drafts.

Nick Sirianni wanted better detail. He saw another Eagles loss: ‘That’s my freaking job’ – The Athletic

Of course, Sirianni did not coach Markel Bell to move before the snap or Mailata to line up incorrectly or Elliott to miss a makable field goal. But it all funnels up to the head coach. He bears the public onus because that’s what he views as the coach’s responsibility, but it truly is his responsibility. “Every product on that field — Offense, defense, special teams, fundamentals, situational football, player making a mistake, coach making a mistake — that’s my freaking job,” Sirianni said. “And so I’m pissed at myself, and I know I’ll fight like hell to do everything I can to get it fixed.”

Nick Sirianni: We’re going to ‘continue to fight’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

“We need to get better as a whole,” Sirianni said. “I got a lot of faith in everybody in that locker room. I got a lot of faith in the coaches in that locker room. I know we got a bunch of guys who will fight regardless of the circumstances.”

Saints move on from run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti – Canal Street Chronicles

When the Saints hired Paganetti, it seemed like an excellent move because of his role in building the historic Super Bowl-winning Philadelphia Eagles’ offensive line. That impact was supposed to carry over to the Saints’ offensive line and running game, but as we know, those expectations fell short.

Giants vs. Eagles odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup – Big Blue View

This marks just the second time in 2026 that the Giants open a week as favorites. It’s a shocking development that nobody would have seen coming at the start of the year that the Giants are actually favored in Philadelphia. The Giants are coming off of a bye week and upset victory as 10.5-point underdogs, while the Eagles are coming off a sixth straight loss.

Cowboys vs. Cardinals Stock Report: Brian Schottenheimer’s offense shrinks – Blogging The Boys

Stock Down: Dak Prescott. As a whole the Cowboys offense was given the ball six times by their defense and ultimately scored just twice. What’s more is that the offense had 12 true possessions (discounting the kneel down at the end of regulation) and failed to net double-digit yardage on seven of them. 7 of 12! Dak Prescott was under some duress (more on that in a moment), but there is no excuse. The franchise quarterback has to do more.

The Winners and Losers of the NFL Week 8 – The Ringer

Despite all this, Dallas had a chance to win in overtime. It won the coin toss, elected to kick, and finally managed to stop Arizona’s offense thanks to a first-down sack of Minshew. But Prescott got sacked on the Cowboys’ subsequent possession, and their offense sputtered as a result. Thus, they punted the ball away to Arizona with more than seven minutes left on the clock. Minshew wasn’t even the hero on the final drive. He threw just one pass, as the Cardinals offense gained 36 yards on the ground before Ryland redeemed himself by booting through the 42-yard game-winner. The result is a clear disaster for the Cowboys, who came in as seven-point favorites but have now seen their odds of winning the NFC East slump to 27 percent even though the team ahead of them, the New York Giants, lost their starting quarterback in Week 2.

Key takeaways from Washington Commanders win over Philadelphia Eagles – Hogs Haven

The Commanders defensive line was decimated by injuries to their two best players, with Daron Payne suffering a season-ending foot fracture on Friday and Javon Kinlaw out for Sunday with a knee problem. Despite the fact one of the team’s best position groups absorbed some huge hits, the line’s healthy members came up big in this one.

The NFL’s overpaid QB problem – SB Nation

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers did something historic on Sunday afternoon: Winning a game where the quarterback was utterly inconsequential. It was the first time since 1974 that a team won a game when the team didn’t complete a single pass, as Baker Mayfield’s job was tantamount to a server, carrying a meal from the pass to a customer. Tampa won because of its run game. Not every team can rely on getting over 300 yards on the ground, or flourishing in horrible conditions — but the Mayfield’s complete lack of impact underscored a larger issue we’re seeing around the league right now, which is that the vast majority of quarterbacks are being woefully overpaid for a lack of impact. There are 13 quarterbacks currently in the league who account for a $30M cap hit or more on their respective teams. The vast majority of those players have been incredibly mediocre this season, to the point where they’re really not worth the money being spent on them. Not only are these players perfoming poorly, but the investment made in both direct cash and player support make them detrimental to their organizations.

item.title: The morning after: Steelers have built the NFL’s most dangerous rushing attack
item.description: The Steelers’ run game has become the NFL’s best.
item.content:encoded:
I can’t remember a time in my life when the Pittsburgh Steelers had as dominant a run game as they do right now.

Jaylen Warren had another monster performance in Pittsburgh’s 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns, rushing for a career-high 143 yards and a touchdown on over eight yards per carry. Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a touchdown in his best game as a Steeler thus far. A Pat Freiermuth one-yard tush push touchdown gave the Steelers an even 200 yards against the Browns, and when you look at how the Steelers have performed over the course of their win streak, it’s safe to say they comfortably have the NFL’s top rushing attack.

Despite a slow start in the first two games of the season, the Steelers currently rank third in EPA per rush behind only the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs, and they are ninth in rush success rate over the course of the season. However, if you look at those numbers since Week 3 – or after Pittsburgh’s pair of poor performances offensively when the season began – they lead the NFL in EPA per rush and yards per carry. And not only are they efficient in the run game, but they are the NFL’s most explosive run game.

Since Week 3, the Steelers led the NFL in yards after contact per rush attempt. Jaylen Warren leads all running backs in yards after contact per attempt at 4.24 (min. 50 touches) and he has the fifth-most 10+ yard runs since Week 3 when the Steelers made their offensive line changes on the right side. Maybe the most telling stat, though, is this one from Derrick Bell of Steelers Now. Since Week 3, the Steelers are lapping the NFL in rushing EPA per play. The difference between the Steelers and the second-place Falcons is the same distance as the margin from Atlanta to the 19th-best team.

The Steelers have mastered the art of being explosive in the run game, which certainly does a lot to take the pressure off the shoulders of a soon-to-be 43 year-old quarterback whose receivers are still lacking in terms of explosive play ability. Should the Steelers be able to lean on this run game into January, they can beat anybody.

It’s the morning after game day, and the Steelers are a half game out of the top seed in the AFC.

Welcome back, T.J. Watt

The last two seasons have been down ones for T.J. Watt. After leading the NFL in sacks for a record third time in 2023, Watt combined for just 18.5 sacks over the last two seasons, including just seven in 2025. If there is one person who has greatly benefitted from the Patrick Graham defense, though, it’s been No. 90.

Watt put up two sacks on Deshaun Watson on Sunday, taking his season total to 7.5, which tops his season total from a year ago just eight weeks into the season and puts him at the top of the NFL in sacks – a place he hasn’t been in quite a long time at this point in the season. Among all players to play 100 pass rush snaps, he is fourth in pressure percentage, and his pressure to sack ratio is also fourth in the league.

And it’s not just sacks that Watt is getting. He’s second in the NFL among edge rushers in tackles for loss (9), and his six stuffed runs are third among edge rushers.

Watt has successfully turned back the clock. And at age 32, he’s playing like he’s in his prime.

Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson continue their excellent run

After a very up-and-down first month of the season for the Steeler’s linebacking corps, Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson have been on a tear during Pittsburgh’s winning streak. Over the course of the Steelers’ four-game win streak, Wilson and Queen are sixth and ninth in the league in tackles, respectively. Wilson’s three tackles for loss in that span are tied for second in the NFL, while Queen is right behind him with two. The duo are also both in the top five in stuffed runs over the last moth, with Queen totaling five and Wilson putting up four. Finally, their impact plays are third in the league with 12 apiece, and no other duo in the NFL matches their 24 combined impact plays since Week 5.

Considering how much flack these two have gotten over the last year, seeing them rise to the occasion and become arguably the top linebacking duo in the NFL right now is such a breath of fresh air for a defense that, as a whole, has been dominant.

Quick hitters

  • Since Week 5, the Steelers are third in defensive success rate, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. A true elite unit.
  • Rico Dowdle had his best game as a Steelers. Pittsburgh’s backfield duo has become very dangerous.
  • DK Metcalf: one catch, four yards. Pittsburgh should take a big swing ahead of the trade deadline for a difference-maker at receiver.
  • Alex Highsmith was tremendous. Only recored 0.5 sacks, but had five pressures. Really good day from No. 56.
  • Eight sacks is insane. The Steelers now lead the NFL with 26.

Let us know what you think in the comments. Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

item.title: Jaguars Get Injury News On DaVon Hamilton
item.description: The worst came true for Jacksonville and DaVon Hamilton’s injury.
item.content:encoded:
The worst came true for Jacksonville after seeing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton carted off the field Sunday.

During Jacksonville’s lopsided 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, Hamilton was carted off the field with a leg injury. That injury is now being reported as a torn quad which should keep Hamilton sidelined for the rest of the season.

It goes without saying how big, both physically and figuratively, Hamilton has been for Jacksonville along the defensive line. He’s the anchor for Jacksonville’s league best rush defense, which allows the fewest yards per carry in the league at 3.4 per. The Jags have allowed just one rush of over 20 yards, and are tied for the league lead in rushing first downs at just 30 all with Hamilton in the middle. Prior to his injury, Hamilton had a half sack and one forced fumble on the year as well as pitching in as the team’s emergency long snapper out in London.

The former Ohio State product is also in a contract year, with the Jags able to get out of his three-year contract starting at the end of the season if the injury potentially presents itself as something far worse.

Hamilton’s injury could now force the Jaguars now to make a move for a defensive tackle. Washington’s Daron Payne is off the board as he too is injured, but someone like New England’s Christian Barmore could be someone Jacksonville could pair alongside Arik Armstead during the team’s run at a Super Bowl.

Jacksonville did pick up Ruke Orhorhoro as insurance along the interior and he has played in all seven games. The team could also choose to slot Travon Walker more in the middle. The Jags did draft Albert Regis in the third round of this year’s draft, but he has been mostly inactive this year.

Jags fans, let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

item.title: Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 8 vs. Chiefs
item.description: They did it again. At one point, the Denver Broncos trailed the Kansas City Chiefs by the score of 24-13 late in the third quarter and things looked dire. The offense was stacking three-and-out drives, and the defense could not tackle rookie running back Emmett Johnson. Then it happened. Bo Nix, Jonah Coleman, and this […]
item.content:encoded:
They did it again.

At one point, the Denver Broncos trailed the Kansas City Chiefs by the score of 24-13 late in the third quarter and things looked dire. The offense was stacking three-and-out drives, and the defense could not tackle rookie running back Emmett Johnson.

Then it happened.

Bo Nix, Jonah Coleman, and this Denver Broncos defense stepped up and scored 15 unanswered 4th-quarter points and had an impressive goal-line stand with seconds left on the clock to win the game. Yet another improbable 4th quarter comeback, and one against a division rival in a game with a lot on the line for the Broncos. A loss would have put them well behind the Chiefs in the AFC West, while a win would have put them back at the top of the AFC West. It was an incredible and thrilling comeback victory, and despite all the naysayers, doubters, and, hell, even their play at times, the Denver Broncos are 6-2, the current 2 seed in the AFC, and leading the AFC West.

Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell you which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After this huge win, we have a lot of players seeing their stock go up, but there are a few players who will see their stock trending in the wrong direction.

Quarterback

Bo Nix – Stock up: It wasn’t always pretty or perfect, but it was a classic Bo Nix game. He made some big-time throws in this game, but there were stretches of poor play (by everyone) and some annoying deflected passes. However, when the 4th quarter hit, Nix and the Broncos came alive and scored 15 unanswered points and came back to defeat their rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs.

Yet another 4th-quarter comeback win for Nix, who was dealing with a retired journeyman quarterback calling his play disrespectful and some media asking if he should be benched. Nix also gets another head-to-head win against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The haters are going to continue to hate, but Nix just keeps winning football games.

Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ veteran quarterback.

Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ third-string quarterback.

Running Back

Jonah Coleman – Stock WAY up: After veteran JK Dobbins got some run to start the game, rookie Jonah Coleman took over and never looked back. He played 66% of the snaps, including the vast majority of the second-half snaps, and totaled over 100 yards from scrimmage. His highlight play was a 50+ yard catch-and-run late in the game that led to him scoring the go-ahead touchdown.

Now, the talk that the Broncos may trade for Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall continues, but regardless, rookie running back Jonah Coleman has proven that he will be a key part of this offense moving forward.

JK Dobbins – Crashing stock: Is it over? It sure seems like it might be over for Dobbins. He finished the game with 7 carries for 13 yards and barely saw the field again after taking an 8-yard loss on one run play. Add in Jonah Coleman taking over the game in the second half and outproducing him, and things look dire. Also, if the Broncos do indeed make a big splash at running back, Dobbins time with the Broncos could come to an end. We’ll see, but things are trending in the wrong direction for Dobbins.

Cody Schrader – Unchanged: Was elevated from the practice squad but only saw 2 offensive snaps and 5 special teams snaps.

Adam Prentice – Unchanged: He has his role, and he fills it well. Remains the Broncos’ lead blocker and a key special teams player for them.

Wide Receiver

Jaylen Waddle – Stock up: The stat line will not wow you, but he had a pretty big impact on the game. He caught a touchdown pass from QB Bo Nix and later converted a two-point conversion, which ended up being very important later in the game. He did see his snap count come down a little, but he was likely held back a little bit due to his lingering chest/shoulder injury.

Courtland Sutton – Stock up: Saw 4 targets on Sunday and came away with 4 catches for 53 yards, which included an impressive catch off a deflection. He also drew the attention of the Chiefs’ defense on the Broncos’ two touchdown passes, so he had a noticeable impact on the game.

Marvin Mims Jr. – Unchanged: Sean Payton wanted to give Mims more touches and snaps, and he did. Mims saw 18 snaps on offense, but didn’t do a ton with those snaps. He had 2 catches for 10 yards, 2 rushes for 19 yards, and was solid in the return game. Pat Bryant is eligible to return next week, so Mims could see his role and snaps take a hit moving forward.

Troy Franklin – Unchanged: Franklin played 71% of the snaps but only saw 2 targets and had 1 catch for 3 yards. The playing time is there, but the production is not, and like Mims, the eventual return of Bryant will hurt their playing time and limit their opportunities.

Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He is who he is and fills his role on the Broncos.

Tight End

Evan Engram – Stock down: 3 targets for 0 catches and played 48% of the snaps. He’s out there, but still trailed Adam Trautman in snaps, and Nate Adkins now has 3 touchdowns this season to Engram’s 1. The production isn’t there, and he’s barely a part of the offense right now.

Adam Trautman – Stock up: He caught some passes! Had 2 catches for 30 yards, including a 22-yard catch-and-run late in the game. The Sean Payton favorite led all Broncos tight ends in snaps and catches this week, and he’ll likely continue leading them in this role moving forward.

Nate Adkins – Stock up: The Broncos touchdown specialist added another on Sunday and now leads the team with 3 touchdown receptions this year. He’s primarily a run-blocking specialist, but Adkins knows how to get open in the red zone and has become one of the team’s top red-zone threats this season.

Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Remains inactive.

Offensive Line

Garett Bolles – Stock up: The Broncos All-Pro left tackle continues to be one of the best blindside blockers in the game.

Ben Powers – Unchanged: I did not notice Powers on Sunday, which is usually a good thing.

Luke Wattenberg – Unchanged: Like Powers, I did not notice Wattenberg on Sunday, but I am also no offensive line expert.

Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: Stud

Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: I did notice him struggle a little bit a few times, but overall he seemed solid. Again, I am no offensive line expert.

Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ 6th offensive lineman and played 5 offensive snaps on Sunday.

Matt Peart – Unchanged: Played on special teams.

Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Played on special teams.

Kage Casey – Unchanged: Remains inactive.

Defensive Line

Zach Allen – Stock up: Remains a stud and the centerpiece of the Broncos’ dominant defensive line.

DJ Jones – Unchanged: The Broncos’ run defense was solid up the middle and held Kenneth Walker in check on Sunday.

Malcolm Roach – Stock up: Roach has been excellent and one of the more underrated and overlooked parts of this defense. His sack of Patrick Mahomes to end the game will be on the end-of-season highlight reel.

Eyioma Uwazurike – Unchanged: Played 45% of the defensive snaps and remains a valuable rotational defensive lineman who allows Zach Allen to take some snaps off.

Sai’vion Jones – Unchanged: Played 23% of the snaps and has earned a valuable rotational defensive lineman for the Broncos.

Jordan Jackson – Unchanged: Was inactive again.

Tyler Onyedim – Unchanged: The rookie remains inactive.

Linebacker

Alex Singleton – Stock up: Singleton has 101 total tackles this year and is on pace for 200+ tackles. He has put together a good stretch of games and has been a very reliable tackler for the Broncos. He also had a sack in back-to-back games, and his sack knocked the Chiefs into deep field-goal range, which led to the critical missed field goal by Harrison Butker.

Justin Strnad – Stock down: Strnad has been a solid player for the Broncos, but he had a tough one on Sunday. He had a missed tackle on rookie running back Emmett Johnson that led to a field goal for the Chiefs before halftime.

Jordan Turner – Unchanged: Played 21 snaps, all on special teams.

Karene Reid – Unchanged: Played 20 snaps, all on special teams.

Cornerback

Pat Surtain II – Stock up: PS2 is back and played 100% of the snaps on Sunday

Riley Moss – Stock up: Was fully back from his injury and played 100% of the snaps vs. the Chiefs

Ja’Quan McMillian – Stock up: Played 81% of the snaps and continues to be the top slot cornerback in the NFL with me.

Jahdae Barron – Stock down: With Surtain and Moss back and playing 100% of the snaps and played just 4 snaps on Sunday.

Kris Abrams-Draine – Stock down: Played 0 snaps on defense and at one point, left the game with an injury. With PS2 and Moss back, KAD is back to being the CB5.

Safety

Talanoa Hufanga – Unchanged: He was inactive again but did return to practice and could be back next week vs. the Panthers.

Brandon Jones – Unchanged: Left the game with a hamstring injury, and we’ll have to see his status moving forward.

Devon Key – Stock up: With Hufanga and Jones sidelined, Key played 71% of the snaps on Sunday while continuing his role on special teams.

Taylor Rapp – Unchanged: Continued to replace Talanoa Hufanga on defense and had a few rough moments and should see his role go back to being a reserve with Hufanga nearing a return.

JL Skinner – Stock up: He stuffed Kenneth Walker at the goal line to bring up a 4th down with under 10 seconds left in the game. A huge game-saving tackle by Skinner, who showed off his ability at the LOS. Can he maybe play some linebacker?

Tycen Anderson – Unchanged: Remained a standout special teams player.

Special Teams

Wil Lutz – Unchanged: Went 2 for 2 and continued to be a reliable and consistent kicker for the Broncos.

Jeremy Crawshaw – Unchanged: Was solid once again on Sunday, but did have a few iffy kicks.

Mitchell Fraboni – Unchanged: Good snaps.

item.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Bears and Seahawks battle with new trade acquisitions on both sides
item.description: The Bears offense vs. the Seahawks defense is a tremendous matchup.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks didn't wait for the trade deadline to make major moves.

The Seahawks decided to fix their run game by beefing up the offensive line. They traded for guard Quenton Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler with the Indianapolis Colts. In Nelson's Seattle debut, he'll see a familiar face on the other side. For years in the AFC South, Nelson and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons battled when Simmons was with the Tennessee Titans. But the Bears pulled off a stunning move last week, sending two first-round draft picks and more to the Titans for Simmons. It's a huge move for a defense that needed a boost.

The two big trade additions are an auxiliary story in what was already a fantastic Monday night matchup.

The Seahawks are 4-3 but still a Super Bowl candidate due to a stellar defense. Their offense has come up short in some close losses, with Sam Darnold pressing and throwing too many interceptions, but it's still a quality Seattle team. The running game should be better going forward. Not only is Nelson a big addition up front, but the team should have running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back from injuries for Monday night. That could be a big difference in a Seahawks offense that too often relies on Jaxon Smith-Njigba for any production.

The Bears don't have any issues on offense. They're third in yards per game and that's with Caleb Williams missing three games due to a hamstring injury. There are a lot of weapons available for Williams. The coaching matchup of Bears head coach Ben Johnson's fantastic offensive play-calling vs. the defensive scheme of Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is one of the best of the NFL season.

Who needs it more?

Seattle is on the spot here. At some point, Seattle can't live off reputation and what we think the Seahawks should be. They need wins. Falling to 4-4 in a very tough NFC West would be a tough spot to be in. Seattle also can't afford to drop too many games at home, where it has one of the best home-field advantages left in the NFL. The Bears don't want to lose too many games in a tough NFC North either, but falling at Seattle isn't a terrible outcome. It's big for both teams but a little bigger for the Seahawks.

Key player: Bears WR Luther Burden III

Burden had a relatively slow start to the season, but he has gotten hot. He has 12 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown over Chicago's last two games. The Bears have scored 61 points in those two games. It's not a coincidence that Burden's surge started when Caleb Williams returned to the lineup. It's hard for any receivers to find daylight against the Seahawks. Seattle has allowed an amazing 642 yards to opposing receivers over seven games this season. The Seahawks' own star receiver, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, has a league-best 867 yards already by himself. For the Bears to win on Monday night, they'll need to figure out Seattle's defense, and Burden is the most likely candidate among Chicago's receivers to crack the code.

Betting market watch, by Ben Fawkes

The Seahawks host the Bears in one of the best Monday Night Football games this season. Seattle opened as a 3.5-point favorite at some books, but it's now pretty much a flat 3. Chicago stunned the NFL world by trading away two-first round picks (and more) for Titans DT Jeffery Simmons this week. This will be our first look at how he improves the Bears' defense. On the other side, Seattle has had an up-and-down start to the season, but looked impressive in a dominant 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks have been favorites in every game (going 3-4 against the spread), while this will be the first game this season that the Bears have been an underdog with Caleb Williams starting. I think Ben Johnson and Chicago show Seattle that the balance of power in the NFC is shifting with an impressive road win.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub.

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

It's a fun one to close out Week 8, as the high-scoring Bears head to Seattle and take on the stingy Seahawks. Here are three fantasy themes to consider as you watch the game.

1. Can Caleb Williams solve the Seahawks? The Seattle pass defense is once again nasty, allowing just 5.2 YPA and a scant 72.6 rating. When Williams starts and finishes a game this year, the Bears are averaging 40 points a game in 2026, but no one is expecting that sort of return here. Can Ben Johnson scheme up his third-year QB in this challenging spot?

2. What does the Seattle backfield look like? Journeyman Emanuel Wilson has been mediocre as the stand-in back, but it's possible the Seahawks could have Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back for this game. Who's sharp and who's leaned on? That's anyone's guess.

3. Will less keep being more for Luther Burden III? The sophomore wideout has played on a modest 60% of snaps and he hasn't been peppered with opportunity, but he's drawing an outstanding 10.4 yards per target. If the Bears spring an upset, it's likely they found a way to get Burden open for some splash plays.

item.title: What does Yaya Diaby’s injury mean for the Buccaneers?
item.description: How does Yaya Diaby’s injury effect the Buccaneers moving forward?
item.content:encoded:
Mixed into Sunday’s dominating win against the Atlanta Falcons was the bad news of OLB Yaya Diaby sustaining injury. Diaby exited the game with a knee injury with 6:32 left in the first quarter. Following their edge rusher’s departure, Tampa’s defense didn’t miss a beat. The Bucs’ defense was pristine against the Falcons, allowing just eight first downs, zero third down conversions, and forcing four turnovers, all while holding Atlanta off the scoreboard entirely.

Diaby’s knee injury is hoped to be non-serious, however, even in its non-serious state, Tampa’s edge rusher is expected to miss time. Without Diaby in the fold, at least for the short-term, players like Rueben Bain Jr., Al-Quadin Muhammad, and David Walker will need to step up to fill the void (7 sacks on the season so far between those three).

Tampa Bay, their defense in particular, does have a tough stretch of games coming up— Starting with Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears this week. Ben Johnson’s usage of Caleb Williams will certainly test Todd Bowles’ recent success. In four games played this season, Williams has five touchdowns, 1,000 yards, and just one interception. To his credit, Todd Bowles has been on his game lately. His defense has held their last two opponents to 13 points total and forced eight turnovers. The Bucs have rolled through the NFC South competition so far this season, Diaby’s contribution to that in the season’s box score— 11 tackles, 3 sacks, and an interception.

The team has improved their record to 3-5 and while they are technically in second place (due to Carolina having already had their bye week) the Bucs officially control their own destiny from this point forward.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: "We're aware of what the issues are, and we're the only ones who can fix them"
item.description: It's gotten ugly for the Chargers, who fell to 0-7 with Sunday's loss to the cross-town Rams.
item.content:encoded:
It's gotten ugly for the Chargers, who fell to 0-7 with Sunday's loss to the cross-town Rams.

Despite coming off their bye, the Chargers could not get much going offensively under beleaguered coordinator Mike McDaniel. Justin Herbert threw two more interceptions, giving him a league-high 10 through seven games. He was also strip-sacked, which was nearly picked up for a scoop-and-score.

Having kicked three field goals on Sunday, the Chargers haven’t scored a touchdown since late in the third quarter of their Week 5 loss to the Broncos.

“Yeah, aware of that and keep working, keep studying,” head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters in his postgame press conference. “It's not a familiar position for any of the guys in our locker room, so we're the only ones who can change it. We are highly motivated and dedicated to do that.”

Asked if he’s worried about Herbert’s turnovers, Harbaugh said, “Yeah, we're aware of what the issues are, and we're the only ones who can fix them.”

McDaniel will continue to call plays, Harbaugh said. Though pressed on why he’s confident this group can turn it around, Harbaugh did not provide much of a concrete answer.

“First of all, it's a team effort, and we're going to look at the film,” Harbaugh said. “We're going to address our issues, where we can get better, and just keep working. That's highly motivated and dedicated to getting this right.

“We're the only ones that have the opportunity to change it, to fix it. And that's what we're going to do, go back to work. I have not been in this position that many times either, here as a coach. But I know we have to be dedicated ourselves to getting this turned. That's where we're at.”

The Chargers will be at home to play the Texans in Week 9.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers hasn't been very efficient in Steelers' 4-game winning streak
item.description: Rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings has been a revelation within DC Patrick Graham's defense, according to Pro Football Focus grades.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers avoided scares in their Halloween weekend victory against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, Nov. 1 at Acrisure Stadium. 

First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team jumped out a 20-6 advantage in the first half and stifled Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson from there, sacking him eight times en route to a 27-6 triumph.

The offense, meanwhile, piled up rushing yards. Running backs Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 200 yards, which translated to plenty of scoring amid the struggles on the other side. 

Required reading: Steelers enter bye atop AFC North with all the makings of a contender

Here’s a look at some of the highlights and lowlights from the perspective of of Pro Football Focus evaluators, who study every play on film to grade each player individually. For context, players are graded on a 0-100 scale.

Aaron Rodgers (65.1) 

His metrics have simply not been very good during this four-game winning streak, and the Steelers’ success as a team has come largely despite his lack of efficiency. 

Between Weeks 5 and 8, his 63.2 overall grade ranks 17th out of 27 quarterbacks with at least 100 drop backs. His two big-time throws – ranked among the best throws in the NFL in a given week by PFF evaluators – put him in a tie for 22nd in that cohort. His average depth of target (ADOT) of 5.3 yards ranks next to last. His 26.3% rate of sacks when pressured ranks second only to Watson, reflecting his general lack of mobility at this stage of his career. 

There are some areas where he’s worthy of some grace. Receivers have dropped eight of his passes in this four-week stretch. Only two quarterbacks have been more unlucky. He’s done a reasonably good job of preventing turnovers. His two interceptions were the results of tipped balls that his receivers couldn’t squeeze. And he’s been very decisive, getting the ball out at a league-leading average of 2.34 seconds per play in these past four games. That’s helped him keep defenses off balance and sustain drives at times. 

The full tapestry of metrics, however, paints the picture of a guy who’s increasingly becoming a one-note passer – capable of dissecting defenses at the margins, near the line of scrimmage, but limited in his ability to make things happen downfield with consistency. That’s not ideal for this team’s longer-term aspirations of winning its first playoff game in nearly a decade and perhaps making an extended run. 

Patrick Queen (75.6)

The veteran linebacker’s ability to be everywhere in some games and nowhere in others is maddening, but defensive coordinator Patrick Graham has him trending in a much more positive direction than anyone has over the course of his three-year Steelers career. 

Queen has posted grades of 73.4 or better in four of his past seven games. In those contests, he’s missed just two tackles and generated 13 stops, defined by PFF as plays that result in failure for opposing offenses. In coverage, he’s allowed no more than 56 yards when targeted in any of those standout performances. 

In his other four games, he’s missed six tackles and had just five stops. That’s caused his grade for the season to dip to a pedestrian 63.2. The good news: His overall grade a year ago was 43.5. There was a lot more good than bad, so Graham’s ability to get more out of him in 2026 is one of his major achievements so far. 

Jaylen Warren (87.5)

The astounding thing about Warren’s production right now is how much of it is coming purely as a result of his power as a runner. Warren generated an incredible 118 yards after contact against Cleveland to average 6.94 yards after being first touched on a given play. He’s averaging 4.14 yards after contact per touch overall this season, which would be a very solid efficiency number even if it was merely his raw yards per carry number. Fully 70% of his 704 rushing yards so far have come after contact. T.J. Watt called him a "bowling ball with teeth" after the game. It’s as apt a description as it is vivid. 

Robert Spears-Jennings (71.4) 

It’s time to give the 2026 seventh-round draft pick some kudos, because he’s starting to pile up numbers that are not insubstantial within Graham’s defense. Through Sunday against Cleveland, he’s now played 147 coverage snaps and been targeted just eight times. On those plays, he’s allowed just five catches worth 44 yards. He’s missed just one tackle all season and has already secured his first NFL interception against Cleveland back in Week 4. Graham’s defense has been very good at limiting big plays during the four-game winning streak. Spears-Jennings has played a big part in that from his safety position. It’s still early, but that selection is looking like a true gem for general manager Omar Khan.

item.title: Saquon Barkley admits his body is holding him back
item.description: The Eagles are not trading Saquon Barkley, so they really should consider letting him get healthy.
item.content:encoded:
After missing several games due to a hamstring injury, Eagles running back Saquon Barkley hurt his back on his first play against the Cowboys in Week 7. He was able to play 10 total snaps that game, and was adamant in the days after that he was committed to playing on Sunday night against the Commanders, even if he wasn’t fully healthy.

How much the back injury was impacted Barkley was highlighted after the Eagles second offensive drive in Washington, which ended with the RB taking a direct snap and running it three yards into the endzone for the first TD of the game. After his score, Barkley was moving and stretching non-stop on the sidelines, with the broadcast noting that he couldn’t sit down as he tried to stay loose.

It doesn’t seem ideal to be playing a running back who can’t stop stretching his back muscles.

He stayed off the field for the rest of the first quarter, but did start taking snaps again in the second — and was even inexplicably used to run out the clock near halftime. Barkley was already on a pitch count heading into the game, and played 22 snaps with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown.

After the loss, the RB admitted that while he’s mentally where he needs to be, with the hamstring and back injuries, he’s not physically where he wants to be.

According to reports, and to Barkley himself, the Eagles have stated they are not moving the running back ahead of the trade deadline next week, Nov. 10. With that in mind, and his future still in Philly, the team really needs to consider shutting him down for a little while and give his body a real chance to heal, instead of making things worse for a season that isn’t turning around.

item.title: Drake Maye provides the answer for shorthanded Patriots in Miami
item.description: Maye led a second-half comeback in Miami.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots entered the visiting locker room inside Hard Rock Stadium at halftime trailing 13-3 to the one-win Miami Dolphins.

It was a sluggish start offensively for a group that was down multiple offensive lineman and three of their top pass catchers before losing tight end Hunter Henry early in the second quarter.

It was a sluggish start offensively for a group missing multiple offensive linemen and three of its top pass catchers, before they then lost tight end Hunter Henry early in the second quarter.

But the group still had Drake Maye, and that proved to be enough to mount a comeback.

“You want to be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there’s not a whole lot of excuses,” head coach Mike Vrabel said post-game. “You go out there and you find ways to win for your football team. And I know that that’s one who he is and that’s what he wants to continue to be. So, he just throws to the open guy and controls our offense and gets guys in the right spot. That’s being one of the best quarterbacks in the league, that’s what the job description requires.”

After scoring just three first half points in a rainy Miami, Maye went on to lead three consecutive touchdown drives in the second half to put the Patriots in front.

The turnaround began with a 43-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Williams on a deep post, as Maye and the offense began pushing the ball downfield more aggressively.

“The touchdown, yeah, I think it was huge. We kind of needed to open it up a little bit and kind of break the barrier of getting in the end zone. I think we did that,” Maye said. “I think Coach was just kind of on us a little bit to stop hurting ourselves, Coach Vrabes and Coach McDaniels. So we were just kind of hurting ourselves and killing drives.”

Maye continued to deliver in the second half, capping off the comeback with a two-yard rushing touchdown and a 48-yard touchdown pass to DeMario Douglas. He finished the final two quarters 9-of-10 for 146 yards, with three total touchdowns and a perfect 158.3 passer rating.

As Vrabel noted, it was the kind of performance expected from an elite quarterback. With key contributors sidelined and the offense struggling to find its rhythm early, Maye gave the Patriots the spark they needed to leave Miami with a 24-19 victory.

“Go be the answer,” Maye said. “Don’t wait around for anybody else, go make it. And I think that was kind of the message everybody took in, and we just felt like we did that. It was good to see from those guys.”
